LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Denver is coming off a lackluster win vs. the Chargers, while Seattle looks to rebound after falling to the 49ers Getty Images In the Week 6 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Denver Broncos play host to the Seattle Seahawks . The Broncos are coming off their third win in the last four games, though it required a late, game-winning drive against the decrepit division rival Los Angeles Chargers . The return of Sean Payton as play-caller didn't exactly result in an explosive or efficient offense, but the Broncos did just enough to hold off L.A. and climb back over .500. The Seahawks, meanwhile, dropped to 3-2 after falling to their own division rivals in the San Francisco 49ers . The Niners moved the ball quite well against the vaunted Seattle defense, and turnovers in their own territory haunted the Seahawks and ultimately cost them the game. Will the Seahawks bounce back, or will the Broncos capture their second consecutive victory? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Broncos vs. Seahawks live Date: Thursday, Oct. 15 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Empower Field at Mile High (Denver) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Seahawks -2.5, O/U 40.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Seahawks have the ball Let's start here: the Seahawks cannot run the ball at all. They couldn't run the ball when rookie running back Jadarian Price was healthy earlier in the season, and they haven't been able to run the ball since he's been out. The trio of Price, Emanuel Wilson and George Holani has combined for just 447 yards on 127 carries -- an average of just 3.5 per tote. The Seahawks do not get much push up front, as their backs average a mere 0.69 yards before contact per carry, a figure that ranks fourth-worst in the NFL , according to Tru Media. Their 2.83 yards after contact per carry is more respectable, ranking 14th league-wide. The Broncos will have to be careful there. They've allowed the third-fewest rushing yards before contact per carry in the league so far (0.59), but the most rushing yards after contact (3.92), thanks to a sky-high avoided tackle rate by enemy backs (30.1%). Much of that production came from Kenneth Walker III in the season opener, but even in Weeks 2 through 5, the Broncos rank in the bottom third of the league in both yards after contact per attempt and broken tackle rate. Wilson is likely to be the primary runner once again while Price and Zach Charbonnet remain sidelined. The Broncos will have to get him on the ground on the first try, limiting the yards he can gain after contact, because the Seahawks just don't create much for him in the first place. He scarcely gets more than is blocked without breaking through tackles. In the passing game, Sam Darnold has struggled to replicate last year's results -- especially over the last two weeks. In games against the Chargers and 49ers, Darnold went just 31-of-51 for 363 yards, three touchdowns and three interceptions. After leading the league in turnovers last season, Darnold has already been picked off five times in his three full appearances this season, while his yards per attempt average is down from 8.5 to just 7.7. His completion rate is down over 3 percentage points as well. Denver's pass defense has been largely good so far this year, with the Broncos ranking fifth in opponents' EPA per dropback, according to Tru Media. The Broncos just held the Chargers to 82 net passing yards last week, which plays a huge role in that figure, but they've also allowed only one team ( Rams ) to top 218 net passing yards in any game so far. (The Chiefs didn't have to throw the ball very much in Week 1, though, because they did whatever they wanted on the ground.) The Broncos won't have Patrick Surtain II or Talanoa Hufanga here, and Riley Moss is listed as questionable -- all of which is a significant issue when you're going up against Jaxon Smith-Njigba , who leads the NFL in both receiving yards and receiving touchdowns. Jahdae Barron and Kris Abrams-Draine figure to see increased roles due to the cornerback injuries, while Devon Key will play more in the wake of Hufanga's absence. They'll all have their work cut out for them against JSN. The Seahawks really don't throw the ball to anyone else all that often. When the Broncos have the ball Denver might have gotten a win last week, but Sean Payton's return as play-caller didn't have much to do with it. The Broncos entered the game against the Chargers averaging a miserable 4.9 yards per play, then averaged a mere 3.9 per play in the win over Los Angeles. Bo Nix totaled just 123 yards on his 27 pass attempts, J.K. Dobbins ran for only 68 yards on his 18 carries, Jaylen Waddle caught just two of five balls thrown his way for just 19 yards ... nothing went well offensively. And nothing has gone right pretty much all year, with the exception of the second halves of the Broncos' wins over the Jaguars and Rams in Weeks 2 and 3. Two good halves in five weeks isn't much to write home about, even if those halves helped the Broncos steal a pair of wins and arrive at 3-2. Nix is essentially refusing to push the ball down the field so far this season. His average air yards per attempt in each of his first two years of his career was 7.3, according to Tru Media, but that figure has dropped all the way to 5.2 this year. He threw deep on 13.1% of his passes as a rookie and 11.8% of them last year, but he's done so on only 7.4% of his attempts this season. Nix also isn't running anymore. He scrambled 27.3% of the time when pressured during his rookie season and 16.1% of the time last season. That number is all the way down to 5.6% so far this year, meaning he's scrambled only four times in five games. All of this, combined with his insistence on checking down repeatedly, has made the pass offense feel neutered to date. Meanwhile, the Broncos also can't run the ball. Dobbins looks like he's running with a piano on his back, slogging his way to 3.6 yards per carry. RJ Harvey barely gets opportunities, but he hasn't done any better at only 3.7 yards per carry. Harvey is at least productive in the short passing game, but the Broncos de-emphasized that last week under Payton in favor of more Dobbins runs that went nowhere. The Seahawks have largely been their usual selves defensively through the first five weeks of the season. They've arrived at their two losses largely by virtue of their offense repeatedly turning the ball over against the Commanders (three times) and 49ers (four, including a fumble that resulted in a touchdown). Seattle has held opponents to the fewest passing yards in the league and the fewest net yards per attempt, and it has limited running games to the eighth-fewest yards per attempt as well. It's hard to see the Broncos snapping out of their funk against this unit. Sean Payton's return to calling plays may have let the Broncos come away with a win, but it did not result in their offense looking competent. They averaged just 3.9 yards per play against what had previously been a very bad Chargers defense. I cannot rightly expect the Broncos to get anything going against this hellacious Seattle defense. It's not like the Broncos are going to do what the 49ers did. Denver is also still banged up defensively and likely won't have Surtain here, which is obviously a problem against JSN. away.headline: Week 6 Injury Report: Seahawks at Broncos
away.blurb: Among those practicing fully on Wednesday was receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who was listed as limited the previous two days because of an ankle injury. Smith-Njigba, who leads the NFL in receiving yards and receiving touchdowns, does not have a game status on the final injury report, meaning he is good to go. Also without a status, despite being listed as limited all week with an ankle injury, is defensive lineman Leonard Williams, who played last week through the injury he suffered in a Week 4 win over the Chargers. Also ruled out are linebacker Chazz Surratt, who will miss a third straight game with a calf injury, and running back Zach Charbonnet, who remains on the physically unable to perform list as he works his way back from the torn ACL he suffered in last season's Divisional Round win over the 49ers. For the Broncos, All-Pro cornerback Patrick Surtain II has been ruled out with an ankle injury, as has starting safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle). Starting cornerback Riley Moss, who missed last weekend's game with a rib injury, is questionable after being listed as limited in practice all week. RB Zach Charbonnet (knee, limited participation) CB Riley Moss (ribs, limited participation) Tuesday's injury report, which like Monday's is an estimation of participation, was mostly unchanged from a day earlier. Guard Beau Stephens (shoulder) went from being listed as limited Monday to full participation Tuesday, while every other player's status stayed the same. Jaxon Smith-Njigba, the NFL's leading receiver, was listed as limited for the second straight day due to an ankle injury, as was defensive tackle Leonard Williams. Wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba (ankle) was limited Monday and Tuesday before returning to full participation Wednesday. He carries no game designation and is expected to play. Quarterback Drew Lock (right forearm) and defensive tackle Leonard Williams (ankle) were limited throughout the week but also carry no game designations. Denver will be without two key defensive starters Thursday night, with cornerback Patrick Surtain (ankle) and safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) both ruled out. Cornerback Riley Moss (ribs) is also questionable after being limited throughout the week, creating additional uncertainty in Denver's defensive backfield. Denver's secondary injuries are particularly concerning against a Seattle passing offense that will have Jaxon Smith-Njigba available. The Broncos have the healthier offense, but the absence of Surtain and Hufanga, along with Moss' questionable designation, gives Seattle a potential matchup advantage through the air. Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans confirmed earlier this week that Harrison Jr. would be making the trip overseas for this week's matchup, and would be due to play a certain number of snaps. But how Harrison Jr.'s first game against the Jaguars could fare has the chance to go a few different directions. After all, it's a very quick turnaround for any player to make when being traded and dropped onto a new team in a week's span, and could lead to his performance in Week 6 being a bit more limited compared to how things might look a little later into the season. So how might Harrison Jr.'s stat line look by the end of Week 6's matchup over the pond? Let's simply predict how the Texans' newest receiver could do in his official debut, and break down just how limited he could be in the offensive game plan. Predicted Stat Line: 30% snap share, 4 TAR, 3 REC, 43 YDS, 1 TD DeMeco Ryans emphasized earlier this week that Harrison Jr. would be involved in the Texans' offense as soon as this weekend. However, he also made sure to note that he won't be expected to play a super high number of snaps . "Don't expect him to come out and play all 60 snaps in the game," Ryans said on Wednesday. "But we'll make sure he gets what he needs, and make sure he's confident in what we're asking him to do." So just how many snaps could Harrison Jr. play? One outcome that could make sense is simply putting him in the role that now-former Texans wideout Jared Wayne had been in for the first few weeks. Jared Wayne and Marvin Harrison Jr. are vastly different talents, let's be clear. picks.headline: Jaguars-Texans Week 6 national predictions roundup: AFC South hierarchy officially at stake
picks.blurb: JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars know just how much is at stake entering Week 6. The Jaguars have a long season to go after their first brush with the Houston Texans on Sunday, but that doesn't take away the importance of a rivalry AFC South game that could heavily impact where each team goes from here. As Jaguars head coach Liam Coen noted this week, divisional games offer a chance for a different slate of circumstances compared to typical weeks. "Know that every time that you line up against this team, it's going to be a fight. It's going to be a brawl. That's what's great about football, that's what's great about rivalries, is that you have a level of respect for each other," Coen said. "Because you know any given Sunday, anything can happen, especially in rivalry-type games and understanding what you can learn from each of these opportunities that you play against one another in, and how well you start to get to know each other in ways in terms of what they want to do, what we want to do. And that's the cat and mouse game; that's the game within the game that you have to play.” So with the Jaguars and Texans seemingly so evenly matched entering Week 6, how does the national media see this game playing out? We break it down below. National Media Picks Sports Illustrated Albert Breer: Texans Eva Geitheim: Jaguars Mitch Goldich: Jaguars Mike Kadlick: Jaguars Gilbert Manzano: Jaguars Conor Orr: Texans John Pluym: Jaguars Matt Verderame: Jaguars Pamela Maldonado: Texans Eric Moody: Jaguars Seth Walder: Texans Jeremy Bergman: Texans Brooke Cersosimo: Jaguars Gennaro Filice: Texans Bobby Kownack: Jaguars Dan Parr: Jaguars Zach Berman: Texans Jon Greenberg: Texans Larry Holder: Jaguars Chad Graff: Texans Josh Kendall: Jaguars Austin Mock: Jaguars Steven Louis Goldstein: Jaguars Jacksonville Jaguars On SI Analysis Jaguars get the nod over Houston 14-9, making this their second-tightest voting split this year after their Week 2 game against the Denver Broncos. This is not exactly surprising considering the Jaguars and Texans played each other so tightly two years ago, and considering the fact that so many had picked the Texans to win the AFC South to begin with. Houston just needed one win against the hapless Titans to draw closer to the Jaguars in terms of votes. I think this will be a close game because, on paper, these two teams are close in nearly every area. The Jaguars have a much better running game than the Texans do, but both teams have talented quarterbacks who are playing well, proven head coaches, explosive pass-catchers, strong defenses, so on and so forth. Even the biggest question for each team is the same (the offensive lines). While the Texans are 1-4, everything indicates this is a closer matchup on paper than one would think just looking at the records. With that said, I think the fact the Jaguars have been a more complete team this season is no accident and is not owrth simply tossing aside. The Jaguars have been one of the best teams in the NFL this season, and the Jaguars have more things to hang their hat on right now than this Texans squad does. I have the Jaguars 27, Texans 24 in what should be another one-score game that gets decided with a late score or stop. picks.blurb: Texans vs. Jaguars bold predictions for NFL London Game in Week 6 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Fantasy Basketball Sign Up ALCS Game 4 postponed Ryan Fitzpatrick rips Bo Nix How WNBA Finals will be won Texans vs. Jaguars bold predictions for NFL London Game in Week 6 Garrett Kerman, ClutchPoints Tue, October 13, 2026 at 6:02 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars meet Sunday at Wembley Stadium with records that suggest a mismatch: Houston is 1-4, while Jacksonville is 4-1. But the numbers beneath those records leave room for a considerably less predictable afternoon in London. Jacksonville enters as a 2.5-point favorite after escaping Philadelphia 19-17. Houston finally broke through by beating Tennessee 26-3, then acquired Marvin Harrison Jr. These predictions deliberately push beyond a narrow upset or another respectable quarterback performance. The forecast: Houston produces its most complete game of the season. CJ Stroud throws for 350 yards and four touchdowns Corey Perrine/Florida Times-Union / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images Jacksonville's defense allows only 14 points per game, second in the NFL. Predicting four passing touchdowns against that unit is aggressive, but its strength against the run can obscure a vulnerable pass defense. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Jaguars surrender 277.2 passing yards per game, ranking 30th. Conversely, they allow an NFL-best 63.8 rushing yards per game and just 2.9 yards per carry. Houston therefore has good reason to attack through Stroud rather than repeatedly challenge Jacksonville's strongest area. Stroud has already thrown for 1,402 yards with six touchdowns and no interceptions through five games. Against Tennessee, he completed 26 of 34 attempts for 261 yards, including an impressive eight completions on 11 pressured throws for 115 yards. The prediction requires Houston to convert passing volume into touchdowns, something it has not consistently accomplished. Harrison's arrival creates another possible weapon, although his debut and workload remain uncertain. This call rests primarily on Stroud's existing production and Jacksonville's passing-yardage vulnerability, not an assumption that the newcomer immediately dominates. Will Anderson Jr. records four sacks as Houston forces three turnovers Anderson delivered three of Houston's four sacks against Tennessee, providing the foundation for an even bigger prediction against Jacksonville. Four sacks by one player would be a spectacular follow-up, not merely continued improvement. The Texans limited the Titans to 187 total yards and three points after DeMeco Ryans reclaimed defensive play-calling duties. Tennessee's struggling offense makes that result an imperfect measuring stick, but Houston still ranks ninth in yards allowed per play. Jacksonville presents a tougher opponent, yet Sunday exposed pressure points. Trevor Lawrence threw an interception and lost a fumble against Philadelphia despite producing 331 passing yards and two touchdowns. Houston must turn disruptive plays into possession changes, rather than simply allowing Jacksonville to reset after sacks. The Jaguars' penalty problems could help create those opportunities. They have committed at least 13 penalties and accumulated more than 100 penalty yards in consecutive games. Backward movement makes passing situations more predictable, giving Anderson additional chances to attack. The bold call is four Anderson sacks and three Houston takeaways: pressure converts Jacksonville's mistakes into decisive field-position advantages. The Texans win by at least 17 points Jacksonville's winning record and scoring defense make a comfortable Houston victory the biggest leap here. The Jaguars have allowed only 70 points across five games, while the Texans entered last Sunday without a win. Nevertheless, a blowout becomes plausible if the first two predictions connect. Houston's passing offense attacks Jacksonville's statistical weakness, while turnovers supply short fields and prevent Lawrence from answering every score. Jacksonville also needed a 53-yard kickoff return and Cam Little's 57-yard field goal to escape Philadelphia. That extraordinary finish demonstrated resilience, but it should not conceal how close the Jaguars came to losing. Stroud's four touchdown passes power the offense, and defensive disruption keeps the Jaguars from turning their rushing balance into sustained control. London delivers a division-changing upset, not another last-second escape. home.headline: Jaguars turn to Jacob Bobenmoyer after Ross Matiscik injury: Report
home.blurb: NFL MLB NBA NHL NCAA Football NCAA Basketball UFC/MMA PGA Tour Games JACKSONVILLE JAGUARS Jaguars sign Jacob Bobenmoyer to practice squad after Matiscik injury Jacob Bobenmoyer will take over snapping duties after DaVon Hamilton's emergency stint, per report. This story was updated to add new information. The Jacksonville Jaguars have found a replacement for defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton , who served as the team's long snapper for most of Week 5 against the Philadelphia Eagles in London. Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said Monday that the long snapper was arriving shortly, and he's now at The Grove with the rest of the team. According to NFL Media's Ian Rapoport, the Jaguars will sign veteran long snapper Jacob Bobenmoyer , while typical starting long snapper Ross Matiscik recovers from a shoulder injury sustained in the first quarter against Philly. Who is long snapper Jacob Bobenmoyer, Ross Matiscik's replacement? Bobenmoyer, 29, has spent seven years in the NFL with two teams: the Denver Broncos (2019-2022) and the Las Vegas Raiders (2023-2025). Bobenmoyer has played 97 games, recording 22 tackles and 1 fumble recovery. Jacksonville is currently overseas in London as it prepares to play its second of two matchups across the pond. The Jaguars will take on the Houston Texans in Week 6. According to Rapoport, Bobenmoyer has already flown to London. Hamilton stepped in for Jacksonville after Matiscik was injured. Teams typically carry only one long snapper on their 53-man roster or practice squad. Sunday's win marked the second time Hamilton served as the team's long snapper after Matiscik's injury. Hamilton helped set up Cam Little 's game-winning 57-yard field goal . Although Hamilton's snap was high, punter Logan Cooke got the ball down quickly, giving Little time to boot it through the uprights. The Jaguars won in the final seconds against the Eagles, 19-17. The Jaguars (4-1) will face off against the Texans in Week 6 at Wembley Stadium as they look to bury their division rival. The Texans are currently 1-4 after netting their first win over the Tennessee Titans in Week 5. Demetrius Harvey is the Jacksonville Jaguars reporter for the Florida Times-Union. You can follow him on X (formerly Twitter) at @Demetrius82 or on Bluesky at Demetrius .

The Atlanta Falcons received good news on Michael Penix Jr. before Week 6. Penix fully participated in Friday's practice and has no game designation on Atlanta's injury report . Barring a setback, the quarterback should start Sunday's game against the Chicago Bears. Penix suffered a rib injury after taking a hard hit in the fourth quarter of Monday night's loss to the Baltimore Ravens. He returned shortly after the hit, but Tua Tagovailoa replaced the former first-round pick in overtime. "They're good," Penix said of his ribs, per ESPN's Marc Raimondi . "They get better every day. I felt good today at practice, and I know I'm going to continue to feel good. I just got to stay on top of my rehab and just make sure I'm doing all the right things." Recovering from a torn ACL, Penix missed the first two games of the 2026 season. He showed no rust in his comeback, leading the Falcons to back-to-back road wins over the Green Bay Packers and New Orleans Saints. Penix has looked sharp running Stefanski's offense, completing 52 of 77 passes for 719 yards, three touchdowns, and one interception with a 104.8 quarterback rating. He watched Tagovailoa throw an interception to end Monday night's home loss to the Ravens, who were playing without Lamar Jackson.

away.headline: Chicago Bears DE Montez Sweat suspended for violating NFL performance-enhancing substances policy
away.blurb: Updated on: October 13, 2026 / 3:19 PM CDT / CBS Chicago Chicago Bears defensive end Montez Sweat is suspended for the team's next two games without pay for violating the NFL's performance-enhancing substances policy, the NFL said Tuesday. The NFL did not specify further details about what Sweat is accused of doing or what kind of drugs he is accused of taking. This means Sweat will not play with the Bears when they take on the Atlanta Falcons this coming Sunday, nor when they take on the New England Patriots on Thursday of next week. He will be eligible for reinstatement on Friday, Oct. 23, after the Bears-Patriots game. In the next game after that, the Bears take on the Seattle Seahawks. The Bears acquired the rusher Sweat from the Washington Commanders in the fall of 2023.

Penix suffered a rib injury after taking a hard hit in the fourth quarter of Monday night's loss to the Baltimore Ravens. Recovering from a torn ACL, Penix missed the first two games of the 2026 season. He watched Tagovailoa throw an interception to end Monday night's home loss to the Ravens, who were playing without Lamar Jackson.

home.headline: Atlanta Falcons injury report: Penix in, Henderson out
home.blurb: The Atlanta Falcons submitted their final injury report of the week on Friday. While the list isn’t long, it does feature starting cornerback C.J. Henderson, who has been ruled out for Sunday’s contest against the Chicago Bears with a groin injury suffered last week against Baltimore. Outside of Henderson, the Falcons injury report is pretty clean, with only defensive end Za’Darius Smith listed as questionable with a neck injury he’s been dealing with for a couple of weeks. Smith cleared concussion protocol Thursday, making him available Sunday if the team decides his neck is ready. Penix was knocked out of Sunday night’s game against the Baltimore Ravens after taking a big hit to his ribs. He was replaced by Tua Tagovailoa, who threw a game-sealing interception in a losing effort in overtime. “I hated it,” Penix said of being on the sideline during the game’s final moments. “I hated that I couldn’t get back in that game. With Henderson sidelined, Atlanta will turn to Mike Hughes and Avieon Terrell for help on the outside this week against the Bears. Defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich expressed confidence in those guys on Thursday, foreshadowing Henderson’s anticipated absence this weekend. As expected, quarterback Michael Penix Jr. has been removed from the injury report and heads into the weekend with no injury designation and will play against the Bears. Can you believe it? This weekend, two AFC South rivals in the Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars will battle in London, while Caleb Williams looks to return to the lineup against the Atlanta Falcons after missing the last three games. We also have an intriguing matchup in the NFC on Sunday night between the Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers , while the Washington Commanders will look to get back on track against the 49ers in San Francisco following their embarrassing tie with the New York Giants . Dan Quinn needs to find a way to get his team to refocus after they completely forgot about the clock in overtime. Which teams should you pick in Week 6, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 13 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Houston Texans vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (-3) (London) Dajani (Texans +3): The Jaguars have established themselves as one of the best teams in the AFC. While that's objectively true, they certainly aren't perfect. They probably should have dominated a short-handed Philadelphia Eagles team last week, yet didn't. Additionally, there are some questions about the offensive operation. Jacksonville went 0-3 in the red zone last week, including two trips where the Jags failed to score any points from the one-yard line. As for the Texans, they are coming off their first win of the season against the lowly Tennessee Titans . I predict they keep that momentum going and score an upset victory across the pond. DeMeco Ryans is calling defensive plays again, and C.J. Stroud is actually playing good football. He's tied for the most 20-yard completions (21) in the NFL this season. Houston is also 14-2 SU and 11-4-1 ATS in its last 16 divisional games away from home. … Prediction: Texans 21, Jaguars 18 Dubin (Jaguars -3): I think it's a real advantage that the Jaguars have already been in London for a week while the Texans haven't yet traveled across the pond. Jacksonville, as Dajani mentioned, has established itself as one of the best teams in the AFC. The offense has been efficient and explosive, and the defense has looked good as well. I know the Jags struggled with the Eagles for a bit of last week's game and probably should have lost, but Houston has only beaten a Tennessee team that is barely functional. It's not like the Texans have looked good at any point. Their defense has disappointed, and they can't run the ball whatsoever. … Prediction: Jaguars 24, Texans 20 Chicago Bears (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): It looks like Caleb Williams is going to return to the lineup after missing three games with his hamstring injury, and it also looks like Michael Penix Jr . will play after missing the very end of "Sunday Night Football" with his rib injury. The Chicago Bears have racked up their most rushing yards per contest (173.2) through five games since 1988, but keep an eye on the status of Kyle Monangai , who missed Week 5 with a toe injury. Last week's loss to the Packers was concerning from a defensive standpoint. The Bears have actually allowed 30 points over three straight road games (dating back to last year), which is tied for the longest streak in TEAM HISTORY. I'm going to take the points with the home team, and take Bijan Robinson and Co. to bounce back. … Prediction: Falcons 30, Bears 27 Dubin (Bears -3): The impending return of Caleb Williams has me leaning toward Chicago here. In the one non-monsoon game that Williams played, the Bears dropped 59 points on the Panthers . They ran the ball at will and created explosive plays in the passing game. Their defense was exposed a bit by the Packers last week, and the Falcons could get going offensively here ... if Michael Penix Jr. actually plays through the rib injury he suffered last week. At least some of this pick is thinking Tua Tagovailoa could start under center for Atlanta. … Prediction: Bears 23, Falcons 17 Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) at Cleveland Browns Dajani ( Ravens -4.5): I'm not going to bash the Cleveland Browns for their loss to the New York Jets in that gross weather, where punter Corey Bojorquez missed a snap and granted the Jets 34 yards of field position to set up the game-winning touchdown. But I am nervous about Cleveland's injuries with guys like Carson Schwesinger , Mason Graham , Mike Hall Jr., Tytus Howard , Quinshon Judkins and KC Concepcion banged up. I think it's fair to say that Lamar Jackson is expected back this week after sitting one game with his ankle injury, but I was wildly impressed with this Ravens defense and their ability to shut down what was statistically the hottest offense in the NFL since Michael Penix Jr. returned. Bijan Robinson rushed for 86 yards on Sunday night. He was averaging about 170 rushing yards per game with Penix under center. If it weren't for all the walking wounded in Cleveland, I would probably side with the home dogs. Not this time. … Prediction: Ravens 26, Browns 20 Dubin (Ravens -4.5): I can't tell if this line is assuming the return of Lamar Jackson or not, but r ecent reporting suggests he has a chance to return to action . If he does, I think the Ravens win this game by a lot. The Browns might be 3-2, but they have not played like an above .500 team so far. Each of their wins required a game-winning drive late in the fourth quarter, and that's not at all sustainable. I don't trust that their offense can get anything going given the various injuries to the skill-position players, and if Jackson is back, I don't think the Ravens' offense can be stopped. … Prediction: Ravens 31, Browns 14 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles (-1.5) Dajani (Panthers +1.5): CBS Sports legend John Breech pointed out that the Eagles are facing a scheduling disadvantage this week that no team has ever been able to overcome. Philly is, of course, coming off an international game and facing a team that is coming off its bye. This has only happened four times, but the team coming off the international game is 0-4 SU and 0-3-1 ATS. That's pretty fascinating. The Eagles have covered the spread just once all season, while the last time the Panthers were on the field, they registered an impressive victory against the Detroit Lions . Bryce Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns, Chuba Hubbard rushed for 122 yards and two touchdowns and Tet McMillan caught 14 passes for 192 yards and -- you guessed it -- two touchdowns. I have some legitimate concerns about the Panthers defense, but I'll take the upset in Philly. … Prediction: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 Dubin (Eagles -1.5): I don't feel good about this one at all. I'm basically just throwing my hands in the air and saying, well, the Eagles can't lose again , can they? … Prediction: Eagles 20, Panthers 17 Dallas Cowboys at Green Bay Packers (-1.5) (SNF) Dajani (Packers -1.5): I told you the Packers were going to upset the Bears last week, and that something "weird" was going to happen. The "weird" came in the form of a 31-7 beatdown of Tyson Bagent . It's tough to trust Dallas after watching an undrafted rookie quarterback making his second career start come into AT&T Stadium and drop 419 yards of total offense on the Cowboys' head in prime time. Now, they have to go to Lambeau Field and try to stop a quarterback in Jordan Love , who is clearly finding his rhythm, having just thrown for 367 yards and two touchdowns. CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens are definitely a fun duo, but so are Christian Watson and Matthew Golden . Heck, let's make it a trio with tight end Tucker Kraft . … Prediction: Packers 27, Cowboys 24 Dubin (Packers -1.5): The Dallas defense is just too bad for me to feel comfortable picking the Cowboys against a team that has an offensive pulse. The Packers showed last week that they are capable of throwing the ball all over the yard even if their running game can't get going. Even with the return of Joey Porter Jr. , I expect that Green Bay will get one or all of Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft going down the field. Dallas should put up points, too, because the Packers' defense is no great shakes, but I'm taking Green Bay to win here. … Prediction: Packers 33, Cowboys 28 Washington Commanders at San Francisco 49ers (-7.5) (MNF) Dajani (49ers -7.5): I am genuinely curious how the Commanders running the clock out on themselves affected the locker room. That's something that seems hard to bounce back from, because everyone looks dumb. Obviously, the buck stops with the head coach, but why did offensive coordinator David Blough call a play that USED MOTION as precious seconds ticked off the clock, and how was quarterback Jayd

Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said that Jackson is “day-to-day” with the ankle injury that he suffered in Week 4 against the Tennessee Titans. Jackson did not play in the Ravens’ win over the Atlanta Falcons in Week 5, as Tyler Huntley (three total scores) led Baltimore to a victory – their third straight with him in the lineup for an injured Jackson dating back to the 2025 season. Minter said that Lamar Jackson remains “day to day” and when he’s ready, he’ll be out at practice. There has been a ton of movement in the odds for this game between the Ravens and Browns, as oddsmakers are gauging whether or not the two-time league MVP will play. Sports Illustrated spoke with several oddsmakers to give bettors some insight into how the spread for this game is currently set, and where it could move if Jackson doesn’t play. “The line this week indicates Jackson is around 60/40 to go and a revision will be made one way or the other once we know more on his status,” Johnny Avello, Director of Race and Sports Operations for DraftKings Sportsbook , told Sports Illustrated. “There were no adjustments made with the Ravens winning on Sunday night, since backups don’t usually play as well in back-to-back games as opponents have more time to prepare.” After the Ravens opened as 3.5-point favorites against the Browns on Sunday night, that line has moved quite a bit toward Baltimore. The Ravens were 4.5-point favorites early in the week and moved as far as 5.5-point favorites at home books after ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported on Wednesday that Jackson had a “realistic” chance to play against Cleveland. However, the star quarterback then missed practice, causing some books to adjust the line towards the Browns. “We're sitting at five on our site,” Ty Gour, Sports Trader at Fanatics Sportsbook , told Sports Illustrated on Wednesday. “As it currently stands as of this moment, and as Lamar's status becomes murkier, that will likely go further towards the Browns.” Still, the opening number that books shared baked in an expectation for the two-time MVP to play. Jackson’s injury isn’t considered to be a long-term issue, and he’s been one of the best quarterbacks in the NFL when he’s been able to take the field in 2026. In his four games in the 2026 campaign, Jackson has completed 70.8 percent of his passes in 2026 for 967 yards, six scores and one pick while adding 18 carries for 144 yards and a score on the ground. "Looking at this line, we are expecting Lamar to play," Christian Cipollini, Senior Trading Manager at BetMGM , told Sports Illustrated . "It will drop to under three if Lamar ends up being out. No change for Baltimore, Snoop (Huntley) is a capable backup who has similar strengths to Lamar. They do not need to change their offense when Lamar is out, which is very helpful." While BetMGM has priced Sunday’s game with the expectation that Jackson will be in the lineup, not every book has done so. FanDuel considers Jackson “questionable” in Week 6, yet it still has the Ravens as 5.5-point favorites on Thursday. “We are pricing the Browns Ravens game as if Lamar is truly questionable to play,” a FanDuel trader told Sports Illustrated. “If he is announced in/out the line will move to or away from the Ravens based on his status. Tyler Huntley's performance last week may affect this week's matchup with the Browns, but it will not change the outlook on Baltimore as a whole as their ceiling and range of outcomes is firmly tied to Lamar Jackson's health." Thursday’s practice for Baltimore will likely impact this line, as another DNP from Jackson would be a concerning sign for his chances of playing on Sunday. The Ravens are still capable of winning games with Huntley, who has completed 78.0 percent of his passes for 264 yards and two scores in 1.5 games this season. He’s also carried the ball 10 times for 36 yards and a score. Bettors that want to take the Ravens may want to wait for a more concrete update around Jackson’s status, as it seems pretty clear the betting market has set the spread for this game with the expectation that he’s more likely to play than not. away.headline: Injuries cloud Browns-Ravens showdown for AFC North lead in Cleveland
away.blurb: Browns beat reporter Mary Kay Cabot laid out the scope of the problem plainly. “The Ravens have 21 on their injury report today on Thursday, and the Browns have 17,” she said. “The Ravens had two more added today, including Zay Flowers, who was limited with a toe injury. We still don’t even know if Lamar Jackson is playing in this game and we certainly know that there are plenty of Browns that are still idle, still ailing and not sure they’re going to play.” Still, there’s reason to think at least some of those names could return by Sunday. Schwesinger finished last week’s Jets game. Labbe noted that Schwesinger and Graham are “two guys that wouldn’t shock me if we walked out there (Friday) morning and they’re both in the stretch lines getting ready to go.” CLEVELAND, Ohio — 38 players. Two injury reports. Zero certainty about who will actually suit up Sunday when the Browns host the Ravens at Huntington Bank Field with first place in the AFC North on the line. That’s the impossible situation both teams — and anyone trying to analyze this game — find themselves in heading into one of the biggest divisional matchups of the young NFL season. The Browns’ injury list includes defensive cornerstones Carson Schwesinger, Mason Graham and Mike Hall — none of whom had practiced through Thursday. For a defense that’s been Cleveland’s identity all season, those aren’t small absences. Browns beat reporter Ashley Bastock zeroed in on what the late-week practice absences actually mean in practical terms. “It’s always a little concerning when you get to Thursday and they haven’t been on the practice field at all because that does become a really tight turnaround,” she said. “And I think ultimately it’s why we’re going into picking this game, really just having no clue what to do or what’s going to decide it, because it’s really hard to know those things when you don’t know who’s actually going to be on the field.” The Browns have shown real depth this season. Backup defenders Adin Huntington and Sam Kamara performed well against the Jets even without a full complement of starters. But there’s a ceiling to how much depth can compensate. As Labbe put it: “Your starters and your stars are starters and stars for a reason. And eventually, if you don’t have those guys, that can catch up to you.” The Ravens face their own uncertainty — a reshuffled offensive line, Flowers’ toe injury and a quarterback who hasn’t practiced all week. Friday’s practice will be the key for both rosters. Whatever happens, Sunday’s game may ultimately be decided less by scheme than by which injury report clears up first. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Visit cleveland.com. home.headline: Injuries cloud Browns-Ravens showdown for AFC North lead in Cleveland
home.blurb: Browns beat reporter Mary Kay Cabot laid out the scope of the problem plainly. “The Ravens have 21 on their injury report today on Thursday, and the Browns have 17,” she said. “The Ravens had two more added today, including Zay Flowers, who was limited with a toe injury. We still don’t even know if Lamar Jackson is playing in this game and we certainly know that there are plenty of Browns that are still idle, still ailing and not sure they’re going to play.” Still, there’s reason to think at least some of those names could return by Sunday. Schwesinger finished last week’s Jets game. Labbe noted that Schwesinger and Graham are “two guys that wouldn’t shock me if we walked out there (Friday) morning and they’re both in the stretch lines getting ready to go.” CLEVELAND, Ohio — 38 players. Two injury reports. Zero certainty about who will actually suit up Sunday when the Browns host the Ravens at Huntington Bank Field with first place in the AFC North on the line. That’s the impossible situation both teams — and anyone trying to analyze this game — find themselves in heading into one of the biggest divisional matchups of the young NFL season. The Browns’ injury list includes defensive cornerstones Carson Schwesinger, Mason Graham and Mike Hall — none of whom had practiced through Thursday. For a defense that’s been Cleveland’s identity all season, those aren’t small absences. Browns beat reporter Ashley Bastock zeroed in on what the late-week practice absences actually mean in practical terms. “It’s always a little concerning when you get to Thursday and they haven’t been on the practice field at all because that does become a really tight turnaround,” she said. “And I think ultimately it’s why we’re going into picking this game, really just having no clue what to do or what’s going to decide it, because it’s really hard to know those things when you don’t know who’s actually going to be on the field.” The Browns have shown real depth this season. Backup defenders Adin Huntington and Sam Kamara performed well against the Jets even without a full complement of starters. But there’s a ceiling to how much depth can compensate. As Labbe put it: “Your starters and your stars are starters and stars for a reason. And eventually, if you don’t have those guys, that can catch up to you.” The Ravens face their own uncertainty — a reshuffled offensive line, Flowers’ toe injury and a quarterback who hasn’t practiced all week. Friday’s practice will be the key for both rosters. Whatever happens, Sunday’s game may ultimately be decided less by scheme than by which injury report clears up first. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Visit cleveland.com. We move on to the Week 6 slate, and three writers have their upset picks locked in. Let's dive into them. Gilberto Manzano , NFL Staff Writer Iain MacMillan , Senior Editor, Betting Peter Dewey , Associate Managing Editor, Betting All odds listed are via DraftKings Sportsbook Gilberto Manzano Week 6 Upset Pick Houston Texans (+120) vs. Jacksonville Jaguars First, let me pat myself on the back for finally getting an upset pick correctly. Now that I’ve regained your trust after my Packers-over-Bears pick came to fruition last week, do yourself a favor and take the new-look Texans over the London Jaguars. Houston gained confidence from beating up on Tennessee and landing wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. in a trade with Arizona. C.J. Stroud tends to play at his best when Nico Collins is on the field, but now he doesn’t have to lock in on him with the arrival of Harrison, who played with Stroud at Ohio State. More importantly, the Texans’ defense is back on track, and that could present trouble for the inconsistent Trevor Lawrence. Iain MacMillan Week 6 Upset Pick Tennessee Titans (+260) vs. Indianapolis Colts It's time for the Titans to get their first win of the season. You might be surprised to find out how many metrics these two teams rank similarly in, even some that the Titans outrank the Colts in, like net yards per play, which has the Titans at -0.7 and the Colts second-last in the NFL at -1.6. Another interesting metric for this game is that the Titans have the second-highest run frequency in neutral game states, meaning on early downs in the middle of the game when they still have a more than 20% win probability, Tennessee loves to run the football. That could be an area they exploit in this game, as the Colts rank dead last in the NFL in opponent rush EPA and 30th in opponent run success rate. Meanwhile, the Titans rank 16th and 11th in those two run defense categories, which will go a long way in slowing down Jonathan Taylor, which is the key to beating this Colts team. I'll take Tennessee as my upset pick of the week. Peter Dewey Week 6 Upset Pick Carolina Panthers (-105) vs. Philadelphia Eagles This isn’t the craziest upset pick in Week 6 – Carolina is just a 1.5-point underdog – but I can’t pass up a chance to fade this Philadelphia offense. Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith are dealing with soft-tissue injuries, and the Eagles currently rank 30th in EPA/Play, 31st in success rate and 31st in yards per play this season. Only the Tennessee Titans (0-5) are averaging fewer yards per play than Philly. I think there’s a real chance that Bryce Young and this Carolina offense (eighth in EPA/Play, sixth in EPA/Pass and fifth in yards per play) put up too many points for this Eagles team to compete. After all, the Eagles are 17th in yards per play allowed on defense and 22nd in both EPA/Play and success rate. Both of those advanced numbers are behind the Panthers’ defense this season. If the Eagles didn’t enter the season with playoff expectations, I think they’d be underdogs on Sunday based on their statistical profile in 2026. Plus, Carolina is coming off a bye while the Eagles have a tough travel week coming from London. All signs point to a Panthers upset in Week 6. Following last week's disappointing loss in Pittsburgh, the Colts dropped to 2-3 on the season and are in need of a win against the 0-5 Titans. But will they get it? Here is who the experts are picking to win this game. ESPN's three experts are all taking the Colts to win this game while doing so rather comfortably. ESPN's FPI prediction model also gives Indianapolis a 72.1% chance of winning this game by an average of 6.1 points. Pro Football Talk Mike Florio is picking the Colts to win 27-10. "The Colts can't afford to lose at home to a team that can't do much on either side of the ball." Pete Prisco also likes the Colts to win by multiple scores. 28-17 Indianapolis. "The winless Titans head out on the road to play a Colts team that has been inconsistent. The Colts' defense has improved in recent weeks, which will challenge Cam Ward and the Titans' limited offense. Look for the Colts to get a division victory as Jonathan Taylor has a big game." Almost a clean sweep. Four of the five NFL.com experts are picking the Colts to win. But Gennaro Filice likes the Titans -- here's why: "Admittedly, Tennessee has played like the most beatable team in the entire league, particularly on offense, where the Titans rank dead last in points and yards by comfortable margins. But Saleh's D at least has some bite, especially up front. Jeffery Simmons is an absolute force of nature, and while John Franklin-Myers has yet to validate his $63 million deal as a pass rusher, he remains quite effective against the run. Is it that hard to imagine the Titans containing Jonathan Taylor , getting just enough offense from Cam Ward and eking out a low-wattage win?" home.headline: Germaine Pratt aiming to bring leadership, stability to defense in second go-around with Colts
home.blurb: The Colts are seeking consistency at linebacker, with snaps divided in Week 5 between Akeem Davis-Gaither (52 snaps), Austin Ajiake (32 snaps), CJ Allen (24 snaps) and Bryce Boettcher (11 snaps) with starting WILL linebacker Jaylon Carlies (ribs) out. As with Davis-Gaither, the Colts see value in Pratt's experience not only in the NFL, but with Anarumo's system. Germaine Pratt aiming to bring leadership, stability to defense in second go-around with Colts Skip to main content Primary nav SCHEDULE The Colts signed the 30-year-old Pratt, who started 12 games for them in 2025, to their practice squad on Tuesday. While Germaine Pratt went unsigned up until Tuesday, he found a way to still be involved in football. The 30-year-old veteran linebacker spent time in the summer as a volunteer coach at North Carolina State , where he worked with his alma mater's linebackers. He eventually had a tryout with the Dallas Cowboys, though he didn't sign. This week, Pratt got his chance to get back into playing instead of coaching. The Colts signed him to their practice squad on Tuesday, and while it's too early to tell if and when he'll make his 2026 debut, Pratt said his goal is to use his experience to bring leadership to the Colts' linebacker room. "Helping the defense, just being in this system for so long, that's all I know," Pratt said. "So help it stabilize and settle it down, make tackles, whatever the case may be, get some turnovers." Pratt has played all but four of his 112 NFL games for Lou Anarumo, his defensive coordinator with the Cincinnati Bengals (2019-2024) and Colts (2025). In 2025, Pratt signed with the Colts in October after being released by the Las Vegas Raiders and started 12 games, totaling 101 tackles, a forced fumble and an interception. The experienced WILL linebacker has had over 100 tackles with at least one interception and one forced fumble every year since 2023. "Just adding a veteran presence is big in there," head coach Shane Steichen said. "He's played a lot of football in this league, made a lot of plays, and any time you can add good players to your roster, you want to do that." In the immediate future, whether Pratt could factor into that group on Sunday against the Tennessee Titans – he'd have to be elevated to the active roster from the practice squad – remains to be seen given he didn't participate in training camp and took the field for his first practice of the 2026 season on Wednesday. "I don't know the plan," Pratt said. home.blurb: Colts sign TE Pharaoh Brown to 53-man roster from practice squad, sign LB Germaine Pratt to practice squad Skip to main content Primary nav SCHEDULE The Colts made the roster move on Tuesday. The Indianapolis Colts today signed tight end Pharaoh Brown to the 53-man roster from the practice squad. The team also signed linebacker Germaine Pratt to the practice squad. Brown , 6-5, 246 pounds, has spent the entire season on the team's practice squad. He has played in 94 career games (56 starts) in his time with the Colts (2026, 2023), Arizona Cardinals (2025), Miami Dolphins (2025), Seattle Seahawks (2024), New England Patriots (2023), Cleveland Browns (2018-20, 2022), Houston Texans (2020-22) and Oakland Raiders (2017-18). Brown has compiled 74 receptions for 752 yards (10.2 avg.) and three touchdowns. Pratt , 6-3, 250 pounds, re-joins Indianapolis after spending time with the team last season. He has started 104-of-112 career games in his time with the Colts (2025), Las Vegas Raiders (2025) and Cincinnati Bengals (2019-24) and has totaled 734 tackles (416 solo), 38.0 tackles for loss, 3.5 sacks, 33 passes defensed, eight interceptions, eight forced fumbles, seven fumble recoveries and eight special teams stops. Pratt has started seven postseason contests and has compiled 49 tackles (32 solo), 1.0 tackle for loss, four passes defensed and one interception. In 2025, he started 12 games with Indianapolis and registered 101 tackles (57 solo), 5.0 tackles for loss, eight passes defensed, one interception, one forced fumble and two fumble recoveries. The Patriots are one game up on the Jets in the AFC East standings, and are a win away from making their winning streak three. But the Jets have gotten good play out of Geno Smith under center. "He's done a fantastic job," Mike Vrabel said this week. "And so, if you want to try to create turnovers, you're going to have to actually go out and force them. He hasn't made many mistakes. He's been really good with the football. He’s been decisive, has been able to create some X plays." Ahead of Week 6, Patriots On SI beat reporters Ethan Hurwitz and Zac Ventola break down how the game will unfold, which players will be x-factors and predict a final score. Who do you think is right? The Patriots' defense has helped carry the load this season, and it hasn't come because of the secondary. That unit has dealt with injury after injury to open up the year, and they'll be down Carlton Davis and Karon Prunty once again. Even though New England's offense is gaining momentum, it will be the other side of the ball that will need to shine. X-Factor: EDGE Gabe Jacas One of the players who can truly break out for the Patriots is the second-round rookie in Jacas . He recorded a sack in his first game in Seattle, but has taken a backseat to Elijah Ponder in the pass rushing department since. That's not to say that he's been bad by any stretch of the imagination, but he's yet to have a true breakout game. This can be his shot. Now yes, any given Sunday is a real thing, but it's hard to imagine the Patriots losing to a Jets team that's just been a doormat for most of the 21st century. The Dallas Cowboys entered Thursday night’s showdown with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers as 9.5-point favorites, yet they lost outright at home, destroying plenty of Survivor entries in the process. Week 5 had three teams that were obvious Survivor selections: Dallas, Houston and Cincinnati. They were all playing 0-4 teams, but only the Bengals and Texans came through. Luckily for the SI Betting team, neither of our editors selected the Cowboys this week, meaning that if you tailed our picks , you’re still alive heading into Week 6. Bye weeks are really starting to come into play in Survivor, as the Detroit Lions, Minnesota Vikings, Miami Dolphins and Bengals all won’t play in Week 6. One of the best strategies in Survivor this season has been fading the 0-5 Dolphins, so players will have to look elsewhere on Sunday. There are still some huge favorites in Week 6, the Los Angeles Rams are favored by double digits at home against the Arizona Cardinals, and the Kansas City Chiefs, Indianapolis Colts and New England Patriots are all favored by at least a touchdown at home. Each week, the SI Betting team of Iain MacMillan and Peter Dewey makes their favorite Survivor selections each week to help guide our readers through the season. Here’s a recap of our Week 5 selections before we dive into our favorite Survivor teams in Week 6. NFL Week 5 Survivor Picks Recap Peter Dewey: Cincinnati Bengals (W) Iain MacMillan: Houston Texans (W) Both Dewey and MacMillan faded winless teams in Week 5, and both wins were relatively sweat free with the Texans blowing out Tennessee and Cincy cruising to a big lead in a seven-point win over Miami. There are still plenty of playoff contenders that we can choose from in Week 6, even in just a 14-game slate. Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook NFL Week 6 Survivor Pool Picks Indianapolis Colts Indianapolis is going to be a popular pick in Survivor this week because it’s playing the Titans, but I’m willing to take a shot on Daniel Jones and company to get back to .500 at 3-3, especially at home. Indy is currently a seven-point favorite against the worst team in the AFC South. Cam Ward and the Titans have been downright awful on offense, ranking dead last in yards per play, 31st in EPA/Play and 26th in success rate during their 0-5 start. They’ve scored 20 or fewer points in every game, including three games where they scored 10 or less points. Indianapolis hasn’t done a great job of finishing drives this season, but it has one of the best kickers in the NFL in Spencer Shrader. So, Indy is able to get enough points on the board (like it did in Week 5) even if it doesn’t score a bunch of touchdowns. The Colts are allowing the third-most yards per play in the NFL on defense, which is a concern for them when it comes to this pick. However, Tennessee is 2-8 on the road in the Ward era, and it has covered the spread in just four of those games. The Indy offense isn’t a juggernaut, but it has moved the ball a lot better than the Titans, hanging 30 points on the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 2 while ranking 21st in success rate and 22nd in EPA/Play. I don’t see many spots where I’d willingly take the Colts in Survivor, so this is a way to use them and hopefully advance to Week 7. With more bye weeks ahead, it’s important to save a few top teams – if possible – for a game that may not be as much of a sure thing. Indy at home against the Titans is by far the most favorable game on the team’s schedule outside of a Nov. 15 home game against Miami. The Titans have been lost to open this season, and I don’t expect them to turn things around any time soon with how abysmal their offense has looked. The Colts may not cover, but they should handle business at home in Week 6. – Peter Dewey New England Patriots The New England Patriots proved last week that they still can show flashes of the team that won the AFC last season, especially when they play the weaker teams in the NFL. Their defense is a top 10 unit and Drake Maye can still torch a below average secondary. The Patriots now rank 10th in EPA per play, while the New York Jets rank 20th. New England is also 11th in opponent success rate, while New York is 23rd. That could all lead to big things for the Patriots in this divisional game. The Patriots have a ton of tough games on their schedule this season, including the Detroit Lions, Buffalo Bills, Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos, so taking them when they're at home against either the Jets or Dolphins is going to be the move, which is why this is the week I'll take them at Gillette Stadium against Geno Smith and Aaron Glenn. Plus, New England is 18-2 at home in its last 20 games against the Jets. – Iain MacMillan Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. picks.blurb: Jets vs. Patriots bold predictions for NFL Week 6 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Fantasy Basketball Sign Up ALCS Game 4 postponed Ryan Fitzpatrick rips Bo Nix How WNBA Finals will be won Jets vs. Patriots bold predictions for NFL Week 6 Mandatory Credit: David Butler II-Imagn Images Steve Silverman, ClutchPoints Tue, October 13, 2026 at 5:11 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New England Patriots and New York Jets are both fighting to get their season back on track and both appear to be making progress. The Patriots lost two of their first three games and appeared to be in serious trouble when they got blown out 35-6 by the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 3. Instead of playing like a potential MVP, quarterback Drake Maye had grown skittish and was making mistakes. In addition to throwing interceptions — he has already thrown 7 this season — he appeared to be losing his grip for a team with very high expectations. However, those writing off the Patriots or questioning their quarterback were premature. Maye has bounced back with two excellent games in key victories over the Bills and Raiders. While there are no guarantees in the NFL, the Patriots appear to be back on track and Maye appears to be regaining the momentum he had a year ago when the Pats host the Jets in Week 6. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Aaron Glenn had a very rough season in his first year as Jets head coach, but the defense appears to be very competitive in Year 2. The Jets have an alert and aggressive defense and that is enough to keep them competitive in most situations. The presence of Geno Smith under center represents an improvement over the situation a year ago when the Jets had inconsistent Justin Fields as their quarterback. Getting the best of the Patriots on their homefield would appear to be a major reach for the Jets. However, they were able to close out the Browns under difficult circumstances in Week 5, so they should go into the game with some confidence. Maye will go after the Jets secondary and throw for 250 yards and 2 TDs Maye turned his season around by leading the Patriots to a 29-26 upset in Week 4 against the explosive Bills. The quarterback completed 22 of 37 passes for 269 yards with 3 TDs and 1 interception and also ran for 54 yards. He followed up on that performance with an MVP-level game against the Raiders. Maye threw for 374 yards with 4 TDs and no interception and he also ran for a TD in a 45-17 blowout. There is little doubt that Maye is a better and more confident QB1 than he was after the loss to the Jaguars. However, the one thing that Maye knows is that head coach Mike Vrabel is not satisfied. "Today's not going to matter here in about 10 minutes," he said , per The Athletic. "We still have a lot to improve and to clean up. I'm happy but there's just a lot of things that we have to do to improve." The Jets have the fourth-ranked defense in the NFL, as they are giving up 293.0 yards per game. Glenn has an athletic, hard-hitting unit that will press the Patriots offense hard, and Maye will have to be aware of David Bailey. The rookie edge rusher from Texas Tech has 25 tackles, 5.0 sacks, 6 tackles for loss, 1 forced fumble and 1 pass defensed. He is a game-changing player and the Patriots will have to make sure he can't get too close to Maye. Geno Smith can pierce the Patriots defense with 250 yards and 2 TDs Mandatory Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images The Jets know that Smith is an accurate passer. As they head into this Week 6 matchup, Smith has completed 102 of 147 passes for 1,084 yards with 6 touchdowns and he has not thrown an interception. He has a solid go-to receiver in Garrett Wilson, and it will be a challenge for the Patriots to keep him in check. Wilson has caught 31 passes for 374 yards and has been on the receiving end of 3 of Smith's TD passes. The Patriots have one of the best cover men in the NFL in CB Christian Gonzalez. He will attempt to stop Wilson — or at least prevent him from making any big plays that change the momentum in the game. The key for the Jets in this game may be their ability to maintain possession and not give Maye the opportunity to torch them with big plays. They need running back Braelon Allen to have a big game. He scored the game-winning TD against the Brown with a 22-yard TD run late in the fourth quarter. If he can run for 65-70 yards in this game, it could take a lot of the pressure off of Smith and help him lead the offense to a competitive effort in this game. Jets will hang close in this game, but Pats emerge with tight victory The Jets are a better team than they were last year when they finished the season with a 3-14 record and were a last-place team in the AFC East. They will come into this game with confidence and they should be able to battle the Patriots closely for nearly 60 minutes. However, the Patriots have figured out how to win after their slow start, and Maye will come through in the late stages of the game to get the win in front of the home crowd. The Jets should not be discouraged because they have winnable games coming up against the struggling Dolphins and the Raiders. If they can win both of those games, the Jets will be a .500 team as they head into November. That's significant progress over last year's team and something for Glenn and Smith to build on. away.headline: Patriots injury report: 2 players out vs. Jets, plus latest on AJ Brown
away.blurb: New England ruled two players out for Week 6, and they both field the same position: cornerback. Although they’ll miss two with Davis and Prunty out again against the Jets, they’re officially getting their star back in Christian Gonzalez after he missed the last two contests with a shoulder injury. Although the CB room is looking better, there’s a chance the Patriots’ secondary could be a bit thin once more. Rookie CB Channing Canada (hamstring) and safety Craig Woodson (shoulder) were both deemed questionable. Canada has missed the last two games and was limited during all three practices this week. Woodson, who played 50 snaps last week, was a full participant on Friday. Running back TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) and starting left tackle Will Campbell (knee) were ruled questionable for Sunday after each sustained injuries during the Week 5 victory. The pair were limited during all three practices. The long-awaited return of star wide receiver A.J. Brown could be happening as soon as Sunday at Gillette Stadium. The Patriots ruled him questionable to play after he returned to practice this week for the first time since injuring his ankle in Week 1 and landing on IR. Brown has missed the last four games, which is the minimum amount of time required to miss for a player on IR. His return to practice on Wednesday meant he could be activated to the 53-man roster at any time. “We’ll have to see how he responds from practice today and then go from there,” Vrabel said. Brown was ultimately limited during Friday’s practice, as he was on Wednesday and Thursday. But Brown, who the Patriots traded for from the Philadelphia Eagles over the summer, gives the offense plenty more size and a veteran presence, two things any team hoping to return to the Super Bowl for a second consecutive season needs long-term at the position. away.blurb: Both rookies fully practiced on Friday and appear ready to go. Sadiq was earlier listed as questionable with concussion symptoms, but apparently has passed the NFL protocols. Cooper was on injured reserve with a high ankle sprain They will be needed against the 3-2 Patriots. Once again, No. 2 receiver Adonai Mitchell and star running back Breece Hall will not play. Left guard Dylan Parham is also out, as is defensive edge Joseph Ossai, who has apparently reaggravated his foot injury. Mitchell has since undergone what the Jets have described as a “procedure” on his hand after denying at first that such action had been taken. However, he is still week-to-week, and it’s anyone’s guess as to when he might possibly return. Parham’s knee injury is also a bit of a mystery. He was seen walking around the Jets facility in an air cast, but has not been placed on injured reserve. Big men and knees are tricky, so when he will be ready to return is up in the air. His replacement, Jordan Meredith, has been struggling, yielding three sacks and ten total pressures. Cooper’s return offers intrigue on whether he can provide a deep threat to take the heat off No. 1 receiver Garrett Wilson. Cooper had a 30-yard catch and run on opening day against the Tennessee Titans, pinballing down the field and opening some eyes as to his potential. If he can make a play or two in a limited role, it opens up the field for the other Jets weapons. Sadiq had a big game against the Detroit Lions, winning the NFL Rookie of the Week award. He has since been limited, but his blazing speed always poses a threat that can open things up for others. He joins the returned Mason Taylor as a 1-2 punch at tight end. Entertainment Entertainment Home ··· Boxing The New York Jets will likely have tight end Kenyon Sadiq and wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. in their game against the New England Patriots on Sunday. Of the missing, Mitchell is the most concerning. He will miss his fourth straight game after sustaining a finger injury at a Jets practice. He allegedly caught his finger in a teammate’s jersey, an unfortunate accident that has derailed a promising start to his season. Hall’s quad injury has been slow-healing, but the muscle is one that running backs need to be perfect in order to perform. He will miss his third straight game. In his absence, Braelon Hall has come on strong, rushing for more than 100 yards in his last game and scoring an impressive touchdown run to seal a Jets victory over the Cleveland Browns. By Matt Audilet Contributing Sports Writer 0 Share Newsweek is a Trust Project member See more of our trusted coverage when you search. Prefer Newsweek on Google to see more of our trusted coverage when you search. New England Patriots starting left tackle Will Campbell suffered a knee injury during this past Sunday's Week 5 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. Campbell underwent MRI testing to determine the severity of his injury on Monday. And according to a report from NFL insider Tom Pelissero, the 22-year-old offensive lineman avoided a serious, long-term injury. Campbell is now considered "week-to-week" as the Patriots prepare for this coming Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the division-rival New York Jets. “We’ll see how the week goes,” Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said of Campbell's injury status on Monday. “It’ll get looked at and continues to rehab. Wasn’t able to finish the game, so I don’t know how much time he’ll miss — if he’ll be back towards the end of the week, if he’ll be back Wednesday. We’ll take it day by day and see how he feels tomorrow, see what he does Wednesday, and keep you updated on the injury report.” After a slow start to the 2026 season, the Patriots are beginning to catch their stride. Sunday's 45-17 win over the Raiders marked the team's second consecutive victory and third win of the season thus far. Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the Jets will kick off at 1 p.m. ET.

home.blurb: EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — Left tackle Andrew Thomas (groin), right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor (calf), and edge defender Abdul Carter (calf) all worked on the side with trainers Thursday during the media viewing portion of New York Giants practice. All three, along with cornerback Colton Hood (concussion) and safety Tyler Nubin (neck) were officially listed as “did not practice.” Linebacker Malik Harrison, who was just added to the 53-man roster this week, was added to the injury report with a groin issue. He was a limited participant. For Thomas, who has been managing his injury since Week 2 against the Los Angeles Rams, this has been his weekly routine. He has yet to miss a snap due to the injury. If Carter is not able to play Sunday against the New Orleans Saints, that would be a massive blow to a Giants’ defense already without star edge defender Brian Burns (torn ACL) for the season. Carter has 2.0 sacks, and is tied sixth in the NFL among edge defenders and linebackers with 14 quarterback pressures. Carter leads the league with 11 ‘quick’ quarterback pressures, defined as pressures achieved in less than 2.5 seconds. If Eluemunor cannot play, Marcus Mbow would start at right tackle and rookie J.C. Davis would be the swing tackle. Safety Jason Pinnock, who missed last week’s game due to a concussion, was a full practice participant. That is good news, especially with Nubin trending toward not playing.

LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Tyler Sullivan picks every game on the Week 6 schedule, including five locks against the spread Getty Images I don't know what it is about the Week 6 slate, but I think we're going to have some underdogs bark rather loudly. I have four underdogs not only finding their way into my five locks of the week, but also two of them pulling off outright upsets. Judging by the headline of this article, you already know that the Panthers are one of those dogs that I think will win in Week 6 as they head up to Philly to face the Eagles . While I'll get into why I feel that way below, I'm just as fascinated by what may happen if it comes to fruition. Would this be the straw that breaks the camel's back when it comes to Nick Sirianni's job? Or does he live to fight another day and gear up for a do-or-die NFC East showdown in primetime with the Cowboys in Week 7? Either way, the storylines that could flow out of this upcoming slate feel like they're as juicy as we've seen so far this season, and that's saying something. Anyways, I'll look to improve upon my picks after a lackluster Week 5 where I went 2-3 ATS with my five locks of the week, along with 6-9 ATS and 9-5-1 SU for the overall slate. Note : Cincinnati, Detroit, Miami and Minnesota are on the bye in Week 6. Locks of the Week ATS : 12-12-1 ATS : 33-44-2 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles Sunday, 1 p.m. (CBS, Stream on Paramount+ ) Carolina comes into this matchup with a pretty sizable rest advantage over Philadelphia. On top of the Panthers coming off of the bye, the Eagles were just in London last week. So, we have one team extremely well rested, while the other is reeling and just came off a demoralizing international loss. Beyond the lopsided rest advantage, the Eagles just feel like a mess right now. They're bottom five in the league in points per game (18.4), yards per game (262.2), and passing yards per game (170.6) coming into Week 6. Sure, some of that can be attributed to injury, but even when they've had their full squad, it's been clunky. Conversely, Carolina's offense is top-five in the NFL in those same categories, and it looks like they'll get No. 2 wideout Jalen Coker back for this one. I like the Panthers to roll into Lincoln Financial Field and turn the heat up under Nick Sirianni's seat to a fever pitch. Projected score: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 The pick: Panthers +1.5 Pittsburgh Steelers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers This is another game that has some outliers worth targeting. The Bucs will be at home after an upset win over the Cowboys last Thursday night in Dallas. They'll have the rest advantage over a Steelers team that took care of business against the Colts on Sunday. Similar to how I think the Cowboys sort of overlooked the then-winless Buccaneers with an undrafted rookie quarterback under center, Pittsburgh could get caught sleeping here, too. Not so much because they're going to overlook Jalon Daniels , but the Steelers could get caught looking ahead to their Week 7 matchup against the Saints in Paris. With a France trip on the horizon for Pittsburgh, I think Tampa Bay is a live home dog. Moreover, I think the Bucs defense has a good shot at containing the Steelers offense. Tampa Bay is allowing the second-fewest rushing yards per game in the NFL through Week 5, which could limit Jaylen Warren's impact. Meanwhile, Todd Bowles has some solid splits against Aaron Rodgers over the course of his career as both a head coach and defensive coordinator. Rodgers' teams are 1-2 against Bowles and average just 16.7 points per game. Projected score: Buccaneers 24, Steelers 23 The pick: Buccaneers +3 Tennessee Titans at Indianapolis Colts Sunday, 1 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free) You'll undoubtedly scratch your head at this pick, and it's hard to blame you. Tennessee hasn't instilled any confidence this season and is punting on a league-high 53% of its drives. Still, I think this line is too big in a divisional matchup against the Colts, whom I don't believe are a serious player in the AFC. The Indy offense can't move the ball efficiently, ranking 29th in the NFL in yards per play (4.6). Meanwhile, their defense is 28th in the league in total yards allowed (384.2). Daniel Jones has also turned the ball over more times (7) than he's found the end zone (4) this season. So, for as bad as the Titans offense has been this season, Indy isn't that far off, so I'll gladly put the full touchdown in my back pocket. Projected score: Colts 24, Titans 20 The pick: Titans +7 Arizona Cardinals at Los Angeles Rams Sunday, 4:05 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free) I think we're firmly on backdoor alert with this line. L.A. is coming off an overtime loss to the Bills on Monday night, so this is quite the turnaround for Sean McVay's club. Matthew Stafford dropped back and threw 54 times in the loss, while the Rams offense ran 78 total plays. That could see them a bit sluggish in this contest. I don't envision Arizona pulling off the upset, but I do think they're capable of scoring late to get us within the number here. For instance, Arizona kept the offense on the field throughout a blowout loss to Detroit and scored a largely meaningless touchdown just before the two-minute warning. That's the type of play we'll be looking for them here. Projected score: Rams 30, Cardinals 17 The pick: Cardinals +13.5 New York Jets at New England Patriots I think the Patriots are all the way back. Drake Maye has seemingly returned to his MVP form from last year and just tallied five touchdowns in a blowout win over the Raiders . Gillette Stadium has been a comfortable spot for New England as they're 10-1 in their last 11 home games. Meanwhile, they've also taken care of business against inferior opponents under Mike Vrabel as the Patriots are 11-0 with him at the helm when facing teams entering with a losing record. Further looking at the trends for this one, the Patriots are 12-0 straight-up and 10-2 ATS in their last 12 games as a favorite and have a +17.9 PPG differential over that stretch. As for the Jets , they've yet to win or cover (0-6) a divisional game under head coach Aaron Glenn. And few teams are more disappointing thus far than the Philadelphia Eagles . Might Nick Sirianni get a pink slip if his club loses at home Sunday against a rested and surging Carolina Panthers team?
