High 58F. Winds NW at 5 to 10 mph. With the Eagles -1.5 at DraftKings , 94% of ATS handle is on them but 55% of bets are on the Panthers. There's heavy action on the Over with a low total of 40.5. The latest odds I saw post-Week 5 on the first NFL head coach fired had Washington's Dan Quinn as the +200 favorite and Sirianni next at +400. And that's absolutely no surprise to me after both NFC East head coaches made utterly stupid decisions that cost their teams victories this past Sunday. I'm sure you know by know what happened in Commanders-Giants and Eagles-Jaguars. Quinn and/or Jayden Daniels didn't even get a field-goal try off at end of overtime, with a win in Washington's hands. Maybe that clock mistake was on Daniels, but there's no doubt it's on Sirianni for having Jake Elliott kick off into the Jacksonville landing zone on Sunday in London. That allowed a long return and a walk-off 57-yard field goal to win. All the Eagles had to do was kick the ball out of the end zone and the Jags are at their 35 hoping for a Hail Mary with no timeouts. Kudos to Sirianni for taking the blame, but he wouldn't take any for managing the prior scoring drive in a way that left the Jaguars with more time than they should have had. Two passes stopped the clock, and Elliott kicked the go-ahead field goal with 12 seconds left. Why not run it down to only a couple and make that the final play? "I'm honoring a play call, honoring the things that are coming in the game," QB Jalen Hurts said afterward. "We're not asking him to make play calls in that scenario," Sirianni responded to Monday. Starting to feel a disconnect there? The Eagles' next game is on a bit of extra rest, as it is Monday night in Week 7 vs. Dallas, so you might see a change if this goes badly Sunday, even though Sirianni is 67-33 as the Eagles head coach. That's tied for the fifth-best head coaching record through 100 games in the league since 1970. The team's bye isn't until Week 10, and you can already hear the Mike Tomlin rumors. This marks Sirianni's third three-game losing streak in Philadelphia, and he has never lost four in a row. It's not just his clock management, but his offense has been lousy during this skid in averaging 14.7 points and 217 yards per game while converting just 22.2% of third downs. The PPG is the fewest for Philly through five games since 2012, and the YPG the fewest through five since 1999. A juggled offensive line hasn't helped. With Lane Johnson having retired, Cam Jurgens traded and Landon Dickerson on injured reserve, the team has replaced three starters already. And it's not clear yet if the offense will have tailback and former NFL Offensive Player of the Year Saquon Barkley and No. 1 wideout DeVonta Smith back from injury yet, after both missed Week 5. The Eagles are averaging a scant 3.5 yards per play with both off the field this season, compared to 5.3 in all other situations. It's possible the Eagles are down to their No. 4 tailback because No. 2 Tank Bigsby is on IR and No. 3 Will Shipley was hurt against the Jags. This will mark the first time the Eagles will take the field sitting below .500 since 2021, when they were 6-7. The 76 straight games played without a losing record was the longest streak in team history. The overall NFL record is 145 by the Patriots from 2003-12. Carolina comes off its bye with its 2-2 mark the team's best four-game start since 2021. It's also good enough for the lead in the ultra-weak NFC South – the Panthers are +130 favorites. We get a former all-Alabama quarterback matchup here in Bryce Young vs. Hurts with Young off to his best start and perhaps answering all those lingering questions that have dogged the former No. 1 overall pick. Thanks to Young and sensational second-year wideout Tetairoa McMillan , the Panthers rank top five in the league in scoring offense (30.3 PPG), total offense (405.8 YPG) and passing offense (301.3 YPG). The scoring average is the best in franchise history through four games, and it's their first time averaging at least 30.0 PPG in any four-game span since 2019. Young would make history if he keeps his NFL-best 317.0-yard passing average up, as no QB ever has averaged even 275 yards passing in a season after three straight years under 200.0 passing yards per. Young also led the NFL entering his bye week with 11 completions on deep throws (20+ air yards). He is 0-1 against Hurts in the NFL as the Eagles beat the visiting Panthers 22-16 in the most recent meeting in December 2024. away.blurb: Besides being out of running backs, the other problem for the Eagles is that they've struggled to stop the pass this year and they're facing a Panthers team that is SECOND in the NFL in passing yards per game. I never thought in my entire life that I'd type out anything like that about Carolina's offense, but here we are. The deck is stacked against the Eagles, so I have no choice here; I'm taking the Panthers. PICK: Panthers (+1.5) 27-24 over Eagles However, the Eagles are far from healthy going into Sunday's matchup with the Panthers. Their offensive line is battered by injuries, their right tackle Lane Johnson just suddenly retired and they're down to their practice-squad running backs. Carolina has plenty of injury issues of their own , but at least one analyst thinks they can pull off a win this week. John Breech at CBS Sports is predicting a victory for the Panthers: It's not a wild take given the situation. In fact, they were one Xavier Legette drop away from upsetting the Eagles the last time they visited Philly two years ago. Plus, the Eagles' struggling offense may not be able to take advantage of what might be the Panthers' biggest weakness—their banged-up cornerback room. Even without starters Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson, Carolina might not have too difficult of a time keeping down the league's fifth-worst passing attack—especially if it's still missing their top wideout in DeVonta Smith. away.blurb: Carolina Panthers Injury Update: 2 Key Players Gearing up for Their Return - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Carolina Panthers Injury Update: 2 Key Players Gearing up for Their Return Fans of the Carolina Panthers have finally got some good news regarding injuries. For the past four weeks, whenever the injury banner pops up in their feed, Carolina Panthers fans have covered and resigned, expecting to see their favorite player out for an extended period of time. However, this week, Dave Canales spoke to the media with updates on Taylor Moton and Tershawn Wharton . Wharton had neck surgery back in May, also putting him on an unknown timetable for his return. He was immediately placed on the PUP list, and the Panthers have tried to fill his role as the interior speed rusher. While there has been some success with Pat Jones, who has also missed time, there has been limited production elsewhere. Rookie Lee Hunter has so far been the most effective defensive tackle next to Derrick Brown, but on obvious passing downs, his slow pass rush has been a hindrance at times. In the same press conference where coach Canales revealed that Moton and wharton's windows were open, he also revealed the fate of Trevor Etienne, who began the season on IR. Etienne injured his knee during the final roster cutdowns, allowing Carolina to keep an open roster slot while placing him on IR. He is now ready to make his return. While his production was limited in his rookie season, sitting behind Rico Dowdle and Chuba Hubbard, Etienne played well with special teams and passing situations for Carolina down the stretch in 2025. In a year where the Panthers again lost Johanthan Brooks to am extend groin injury, getting Etienne back to give Carolina running back room of three backs allows for Hubbard and Dillon to get much need resort during games, as well as a buffer in anymore unexpected injuries happen. Etienne will most likely return to his role in special teams, giving Carolina another player with kick and punt return experience to work with. The Carolina Panthers have been an injury riddle in the 2026 season. An early bye week came bearing fruit for the Panthers' injury news. Taylor Moton and Tershawn Wharton's return spells good things on the horizon for Carolina. Moton will allow Freeling to return to the development pool, allowing him to review his film, watch a Panthers staple on the right side, and learn from him. It will also give Freeling a chance to get healthier himself, after suffering a concussion and a knee injury in the last two weeks. Wharton's return means that Carolina might get a boost in pass rush. Wharton has always had the speed and strength to work from the inside, and adding him to a room with Jaelan Phillips and Princely Umanmielen means Carolina will have a perfect blend of speed and power. picks.blurb: Analyst Predicts Steelers to Dominate Buccaneers in Week 6 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Fantasy Basketball Sign Up ALCS Game 4 postponed Ryan Fitzpatrick rips Bo Nix How WNBA Finals will be won Analyst Predicts Steelers to Dominate Buccaneers in Week 6 Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers in a game against the Indianapolis Colts on Oct. 11, 2026 -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now Aaron Becker Thu, October 15, 2026 at 9:38 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads A NFL analyst is all in on the Pittsburgh Steelers for Week 6. The Pittsburgh Steelers are currently 2.5-point favorites for their Week 6 road game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. However, NFL analyst Conor Orr thinks the oddsmakers have it completely wrong. Orr predicts the Steelers will continue their hot streak and dominate the Buccaneers in Week 6. "I wanna see the Steelers go down to Tampa Bay and win another one of these games," Orr said . "I think they can win this game by three touchdowns." Orr has done a complete 180 in just a matter of a week. Heading into Week 5, he begged the Indianapolis Colts to put the Steelers out of their misery. "Clearly you have communication issues. Your coach came out and said your house is dirty and you need to clean your house. Something's a mess here," Orr said on the Heed the Call NFL Podcast . "I'm sick of [Aaron Rodgers]. I'm sick of watching this team. I'm sick of the receivers dropping balls. I'm sick of them having played one good game against the Bengals so we've got to take them seriously for another three weeks. Come on, Jonathan Taylor. Put up 400 yards and put his old, dying horse out of its misery and off my screen." However, after watching the Steelers offense come alive in their latest win, Orr issued an apology to the team and now seems to be a big believer in Pittsburgh. "I have totally done a 180, and I'll admit it, on this Steelers offense," Orr continued. "Down so many people, and even down to Ben Skowronek, this team has been able to find a way to manufacture points. Aaron Rodgers will have bad Rodgers games, but I've totally flipped on this." The Steelers do seem to have some new found life. Rodgers is playing very well and running back Jaylen Warren has been on another level, recording 176, 126 and 188-yard performances the past three weeks. The only question that remains is: Can the Steelers offense continue this type of production the rest of the season? away.headline: Steelers injury report: Pittsburgh enters road trip with abundance of injuries
away.blurb: Out of the bye, road trips to face the division rival Bengals and in-state rival Eagles await. Neither is a long trip in terms of mileage, but the Steelers have not won in Philadelphia since 1965, and it follows an AFC North dogfight. The receivers room is the most pressing problem. Pittman will be out for at least the next three games after being placed on injured reserve. The veteran was a key offseason acquisition but has only played in three games in which he’s caught seven passes for 89 yards. The extent of the injuries to Wilson and Skowronek, sustained against Indianapolis, are not yet known, but McCarthy said Monday that both will be out for at least the Tampa Bay game. The secondary is a bit better off. Ramsey spent the week leading up to the Colts game on the injury report but handled a normal workload. Only Dean was absent, and the Steelers have not yet taken the step of adding the free agent cornerback signing to injured reserve. Dean was a limited practice participant Wednesday while Ramsey was out with a wrist injury listed. McCarthy hinted strongly that Dowdle is expected back this week from the toe injury he sustained in Week 2 against New England. He was also limited Wednesday. That should help the offense manage the reps of Jaylen Warren, who’s handled a heavy workload in Dowdle’s absence. First-year coach Mike McCarthy’s team will play four of its next five games on the road starting this week, and it will take multiple longer – and daunting – trips to do so before things begin to moderate in the back half of the 2026 schedule. All of it will unfold amid mounting absences. Running back Rico Dowdle; receivers Michael Pittman Jr., Roman Wilson and Ben Skowronek; and defensive backs Jamel Dean and Jalen Ramsey have all been hurt in some form or fashion recently. The stretch will be one of, if not the, most grueling in the franchise’s history and could determine whether the Steelers ’ 3-2 start has legs, or whether another mediocre year awaits a franchise that hasn’t won an NFL playoff game since 2017. NFL Week 6 brings a road trip to Tampa Bay to face the Buccaneers . That’s a 1,000-or-so-mile trip right off the bat against a desperate 1-4 team that needs a win to preserve any postseason hopes. One week later, the Steelers will board a long flight to Paris to face the New Orleans Saints in the first NFL regular season game in France. It will be only the second international game for Pittsburgh since 2013. It picked up a win against Minnesota in Dublin, Ireland last October, but the travel schedule was much kinder surrounding that date. The Steelers got to enjoy a bye after their trip to the Emerald Isle and did not need to travel any further than Massachusetts until they visited the Los Angeles Chargers in early November. It was a similar story when they played in London13 years ago. They came home to a bye, and most travel was relatively local for the month before and after. picks.blurb: Behind Enemy Lines: Previewing Rams-Cardinals with expert Q&A - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Fantasy Basketball Sign Up ALCS Game 4 postponed Ryan Fitzpatrick rips Bo Nix How WNBA Finals will be won Behind Enemy Lines: Previewing Rams-Cardinals with expert Q&A Cameron DaSilva, Rams Wire Sat, October 17, 2026 at 12:01 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Los Angeles Rams have their second divisional matchup of the season this weekend, as they'll host the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday afternoon. It's their first meeting with Mike LaFleur's team after he spent the last three years as Sean McVay's offensive coordinator. To preview this NFC West matchup, we asked Cards Wire lead writer Jess Root five questions, even getting his final score prediction (spoiler: he expects the Rams to win big). Do the Cardinals have anyone on offense who can beat the Rams besides Trey McBride and Michael Wilson? Cards Wire: The short answer is no, but other guys will make a few plays. Teagan Quitoriano scored twice last week (his first touchdowns since 2022). Elijah Higgins will be open more as McBride is getting a lot of attention. Kendrick Bourne is reliable. However, none of those guys are players that can be leaned upon for big plays or critical moments. How big of a blow is Jeremiyah Love's injury? Cards Wire: Well, he hadn't been given the offense much overall, but the absence of his skillset will make the running game less dynamic. Tyler Allgeier is certainly capable and Bam Knight has had moments for the Cardinals, but Love's absence makes an anemic running game look even less threatening. Is it still too early for the Cardinals to turn to Carson Beck? Cards Wire: That is the big debate right now. While Jacoby Brissett hasn't been the problem, he hasn't been good, and after going 2-15 in 17 starts for the Cardinals, he doesn't have much of a ceiling. However, the Cardinals gave him a big raise before the season, so they will keep rolling him out until he isn't best option for them. Many want to see Beck, but with only one start in the preseason, no one knows if he is ready or not. What are the early reviews of Mike LaFleur as a head coach? Cards Wire: They are mixed. He sounded good early on, and the offense has had more overall production than last season. However, the defense is terrible. He has become a little less transparent in his answers, and the offense really has been unimpressive with almost no big plays. Who wins on Sunday and what's the final score? Cards Wire: Considering the Cardinals' struggles defensively and against the NFC West, it's a blowout with late offense from the Cardinals. Rams 38, Cardinals 24 This article originally appeared on Rams Wire: Behind Enemy Lines: Previewing Rams-Cardinals with expert Q&A

away.headline: Arizona Cardinals' LaFleur announces Jeremiyah Love injury status
away.blurb: It is not yet clear whether Love’s injury will affect his availability in Week 7, when the Cardinals return home to face the Denver Broncos. When asked whether Love could be placed on injured reserve, LaFleur said “there’s been no discussion of IR or anything like that.” “He's doing good but it's just — you guys see the way he cuts,” LaFleur said. “He cuts hard. That's a superpower of his. And when he's putting his left foot in the ground, it's just not right, right now. And to get him to be to his best ability, it's what's right so he can go out and perform the way that he wants.” Earlier in the week, LaFleur said that Love’s limited involvement as a receiver was because the Cardinals needed their running backs to stay back in pass protection against the Lions. On Friday, he acknowledged that was only a partial truth. Amid a slow start to his rookie season, Love will miss the Arizona Cardinals ' Week 6 trip to face the Los Angeles Rams due to an injury to his left ankle, head coach Mike LaFleur said on Friday, Oct. 16. Love has not practiced all week after experiencing lingering discomfort in recent games. “We knew on Monday after watching the game, talking with him, seeing where he was at, that we were gonna give him Wednesday off,” LaFleur said. “And re-assess on Wednesday, with knowing that probably Sunday was a long shot.” “We've gotta really re-evaluate, really every single day,” LaFleur added. “Not good enough, obviously, right now to go Sunday. It wouldn't be in the best interest of him. And then we'll re-evaluate, obviously, on Monday.” Love suffered a high-ankle sprain to his right ankle on Aug. 13, in a preseason game against the Las Vegas Raiders. He returned to the field a month later in the Cardinals’ regular-season opener. Then, at some point in the ensuing weeks, he began to experience discomfort in his left ankle. The issue first drew public attention in Week 4, against the New York Giants. During that game, trainers repeatedly looked at Love’s ankle on the Cardinals sideline. Afterward, Love acknowledged that the Cardinals have been managing his workload due to health. LaFleur, though, was unsure of exactly when the issue first surfaced. "We just felt like it wasn't improving and maybe even getting a little bit worse," LaFleur said. "So at that point, if it's not improving and it's getting a little bit worse, we've gotta do what's right for the player." Through five games, Love has just 245 rushing yards on 67 carries, for a 3.7 yards per carry average. Love has also caught just 11 passes on 14 targets for 36 yards, falling far short of the expectations with he entered the NFL as a pass-catcher. Recovered from the right high-ankle sprain suffered in the Aug. 13 preseason game against the Las Vegas Raiders , his left ankle has been an issue for several weeks. He has felt good heading into games, but then aggravation occurs on the field. Head coach Mike LaFleur said, “Want to get this ankle right and do it the right way. He’s a tough dude. You guys see the way he plays and how aggressive he is with his cuts. Imagine being a running back in the NFL, trying to put the foot down and cut the way that you’re capable of. We all are in agreeance, as much as he wants to battle through, we’re all in agreeance right now that (he needs to) give a little bit of rest and see as the week goes on what that’ll entail for Sunday.” Asked about concern about it continuing to be a problem going forward, LaFleur said, “It’s an ankle, so you don’t know. I’m not a doctor and each body is a little bit different. The way he came back from the one in the preseason was unbelievable. He doesn’t even feel it, but this one is the one that happened when the regular season started and it’s just lingering.” The full details their Wednesday injury repory are below. home.blurb: Return of Aaron Donald to the Rams defense will likely increase the difficulty for Bills offense to put up big fantasy numbers Add ClutchPoints on Google Mandatory Credit: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images The Los Angeles Rams came into the season looking like one of the dominant teams in the NFL, one that would have an excellent chance of contending for a Super Bowl title. In addition to the outstanding offensive combination of quarterback Matthew Stafford and wide out Puka Nacua, the Rams appeared to have put together one of the dangerous defensive teams in recent memory. The Rams had acquired Myles Garrett from the Cleveland Browns in the offseason, and bringing in the best defensive player in the league got the attention of Aaron Donald . The former All-Pro defensive tackle had retired after the 2023 season, but he sensed the addition of Garrett made the Rams a powerful team with the capability of dominating opponents. Donald was interested in making a comeback and after flirting with the idea throughout training camp, he decided to return to the Rams shortly before the start fo the season. The Rams are expected to have nearly all of their top players available for the test against the Bills. Here's the way the latest injury report looked after the team's last practice session: TE Colby Parkinson, full participation in practice (knee), OLB Byron Young, did not practice (rest), OL Alaric Jackson, did not practice (rest), TE Tyler Higbee, did not practice (rest), WR Davante Adams, full participation in practice (rest), LB Nathan Landman, full participation in practice (shoulder), S Quentin Lake, questionable (hip), OLB Josaiah Stewart, limited participation in practice (groin), LB Grant Stuard, limited participation in practice (hamstring). Rams Week 5 injury report vs. Bills: What it means for fantasy football NBA Eastern Atlantic Boston Celtics MLB National East Atlanta Braves NHL Eastern Metropolitan Carolina Hurricanes While the Rams have gotten off to a halting start — they are 2-2 heading into the Week 5 Monday night game against the Bills — the primary goals remain the same. The Rams are determined to go to the Super Bowl and win it. Donald will give the Rams defense a boost Donald has been working himself back into game shape since he started thinking about making a comeback. home.headline: Jeremiyah Love Gets Concerning Injury Update Ahead of Cardinals-Rams
home.blurb: TEMPE — The Arizona Cardinals are holding star rookie running back Jeremiyah Love out of practice on Wednesday as Week 6 preperations for the Los Angeles Rams ramp up. Jeremiyah Love Gets Concerning Injury Update Ahead of Cardinals-Rams Skip to main content SI.COM "Take him one day at a time. You know, we want to get this ankle right and do it the right way," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters on Wednesday. Love has been nursing an ankle injury through the opening stages of his rookie season after suffering a different ankle injury during preseason. While he hasn't missed any regular season action, Love's participation and impact has been slightly hindered. There's been some talks about potentially shutting Love down to allow the ankle to heal, though LaFleur didn't seem willing to do that. Arizona is just 1-4 and is again favored to lose in Los Angeles. "Listen, I'm going to try to be as candid as possible with also knowing that everyone's listening to this too, right? But he's a tough dude. You guys see the way he plays and how aggressive he is with his cuts. I mean, imagine being a running back in the NFL trying to put the foot down and cut the way that you know that you're capable of," LaFleur said. "And so we all are in agreeance — as much as you know he wants to battle through — we're all in agreeance right now, it's just hey, give [the injury] a little bit of rest and see as the week goes on, what that'll entail for Sunday." Love, the No. 3 overall pick, has 67 carries for 245 yards and one touchdown on the ground while adding 11 receptions for 36 yards and a score through the air. "I think early at his career [he battled injuries], but you had the right [ankle] early, and then now you got the left one. So now you're just kind of — it's just double dipping. The right side, the preseason one's fine. It's the other one right now that's the lingering issue. They're ankles, you know, it's an ankle. I'm not a doctor, and each body's a little bit different," LaFleur continued. "Like the way he came back from the one in the preseason was unbelievable, like he doesn't even feel it. But this one is the one that happened kind of when the regular season started, and it just lingered." Has Love lost any of his explosiveness? "You'd have to ask him that," LaFleur added. "I know how explosive he is. I know how explosive he wants to be. So I mean I think that's a fair assessment in some aspects. Again, I don't think it's an overall hindrance, but again the the rest for him is going to be vital." Kansas City is 4-0 after its bye, while Los Angeles is 0-5 following a 23-17 loss to Denver. Kickoff at Arrowhead Stadium is scheduled for 4:25 p.m. ET. The Chiefs are favored by 8.5 points, but a routine favorite winning comfortably would hardly qualify as a bold prediction. Instead, this forecast projects an exceptional rushing performance, an unexpected Chargers defensive highlight and a fourth-quarter rally that changes the complexion of the afternoon without changing the winner. Kenneth Walker III rushes for 200 yards and three touchdowns Jay Biggerstaff-Imagn Images Walker has already accumulated 537 rushing yards and four touchdowns on 87 carries through four games. That translates to more than six yards per attempt, giving Kansas City a foundation for dominating without asking Patrick Mahomes to carry every possession. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Chiefs average 6.5 yards per offensive play compared with the Chargers' 4.8. Their third-down conversion rate is also substantially better: 44% against 34.85%. Those advantages can sustain drives and produce the repeated rushing opportunities necessary for a monster individual afternoon. The prediction goes beyond another efficient outing. Walker reaches 200 rushing yards for the game and scores three times, becoming the central reason Kansas City controls possession and repeatedly finishes drives. There is an important limitation: Los Angeles allows only 5.0 yards per play, the same figure as Kansas City. This is not a forecast built on pretending the Chargers cannot defend. It depends on Walker maintaining his explosiveness while the Chiefs create an unusually favorable game script. If Kansas City builds an early advantage, sustained rushing volume can turn Walker's strong start into the biggest performance of his season. The Chargers intercept Patrick Mahomes twice, including a pick-six Mahomes has thrown nine touchdown passes against two interceptions through four games, with a 106.2 passer rating. Predicting two interceptions in one afternoon means Los Angeles matches his entire season total, despite entering winless. The statistical route to that surprise exists. The Chargers allow opponents to convert just 31.25% of third downs, compared with Kansas City's 37.04%. Forcing longer, obvious passing situations could provide opportunities that disappear when Walker keeps the offense ahead of schedule. Los Angeles needs more than ordinary defensive stops because its offense averages just 16.8 points per game. A defensive touchdown would change both field position and scoreboard pressure without requiring Justin Herbert to repeatedly rescue stalled possessions. The call is that one aggressive coverage read becomes an interception return for a touchdown, while another takeaway interrupts a promising Chiefs drive. That would be an unexpected blemish on Mahomes' efficient opening month. It would also illustrate why a team's record does not eliminate its capacity to produce a game-changing individual moment. Justin Herbert leads a 17-point fourth quarter, but Kansas City survives Herbert's current numbers make this the most counterintuitive offensive prediction: 937 passing yards, five touchdowns, seven interceptions and a 70.2 passer rating through five games. He has also absorbed 17 sacks. Against Denver, he managed 121 passing yards and was sacked five times. Receiving availability remains uncertain after Ladd McConkey dressed without playing, Quentin Johnston missed the game and Tre' Harris suffered a hamstring injury. Nevertheless, the prediction is that Herbert finally finds rhythm against a defense protecting a substantial lead. Two touchdown drives and a field goal produce 17 fourth-quarter points, forcing Kansas City to finish the game with its offense rather than coast. Walker provides that answer. The final forecast is Chiefs 38, Chargers 31: Kansas City remains unbeaten, but Los Angeles delivers a much stronger response than its record suggests. These are deliberately high-variance predictions, not the most likely outcomes. The underlying numbers favor Kansas City, but divisional familiarity and turnovers can make a comfortable matchup unpredictable. The Chiefs are playing with a chip on their shoulder after missing the playoffs last season, they have picked up wins this year against the Denver Broncos, Indianapolis Colts, Miami Dolphins, and Las Vegas Raiders. Kansas City enters the game at 4-0 after winning its first four contests, while Los Angeles is searching for its first victory after opening the season 0-5. The Chargers will have a difficult challenge at Arrowhead Stadium as they try to turn their season around against one of the AFC's early standouts. Kickoff is scheduled for 4:25 p.m. Eastern on CBS. Patrick Mahomes Leads the Chiefs Quarterback Patrick Mahomes has helped Kansas City get off to an impressive start in 2026. Through four games, Mahomes has thrown for 1,037 yards and nine touchdowns with just two interceptions, giving the Chiefs a productive passing attack. Kansas City has also found success on the ground with running back Kenneth Walker III. Walker has rushed for 537 yards and four touchdowns, averaging 6.2 yards per carry. His ability to produce explosive runs has given opposing defenses another major concern beyond Mahomes. Head coach Andy Reid will look to keep that offensive balance going against a Chargers defense that has shown the ability to pressure quarterbacks. The Chiefs will also monitor wide receiver Rashee Rice, who missed practice Wednesday with a hamstring injury. Justin Herbert Faces a Difficult Challenge For Los Angeles, quarterback Justin Herbert needs to help an offense that has struggled to produce consistently. Herbert has thrown for 937 yards, five touchdowns and seven interceptions through five games. The Chargers have averaged only 16.8 points per game, making offensive improvement a major priority. Herbert has the arm talent to challenge Kansas City's secondary, but he will need better protection and consistent production from his receiving corps. Injuries have complicated that task, with several Los Angeles wide receivers and defensive starters appearing on the team's injury report this week. Head coach Jim Harbaugh must find a way to help his team limit mistakes and sustain drives. A stronger running game could ease the pressure on Herbert and help keep Mahomes off the field. Andy Reid vs. Jim Harbaugh The coaching matchup adds another layer to this divisional rivalry. Reid has Kansas City playing efficient football on both sides of the ball, while Harbaugh is trying to find answers after a difficult opening month. The Chargers swept the Chiefs in 2025, adding extra motivation for Kansas City to protect its home field and maintain control of the AFC West rivalry. A Critical AFC West Matchup Kansas City has an opportunity to improve to 5-0 and continue building momentum after its bye week. Los Angeles, meanwhile, needs a complete performance to avoid falling further behind in the division. Mahomes and Walker give the Chiefs multiple ways to attack, while Herbert will need to deliver a more consistent performance to help the Chargers compete. With the Chiefs chasing another strong start and the Chargers desperate to get their season moving, Sunday's matchup carries plenty of importance for both teams.

Those setbacks have created additional challenges for Herbert, who has been forced to navigate an offense dealing with injuries at multiple positions. Now, Los Angeles faces another difficult test against Kansas City. Sunday’s matchup against Kansas City presents another challenge for a Chargers team looking to gain momentum in the AFC West. Not included on the injury report was Chargers center Tyler Biadasz, who was placed on season-ending injured reserve in August due to a torn ACL suffered in training camp and starting right tackle Rashawn Slater and backup Trey Pipkins, who were each placed on injured reserve in recent weeks due to ankle and knee issues. home.blurb: Wide receiver Ladd McConkey has no injury designation for Sunday’s game, clearing the way for his expected return after dealing with a lingering foot injury. ESPN’s Adam Schefter confirmed the development Friday, citing the Chargers’ final injury report. The announcement comes after McConkey was limited during practice Wednesday and Thursday while continuing to recover from an injury that has affected his availability in recent weeks. McConkey was listed as questionable ahead of last Sunday’s matchup against the Denver Broncos. Although he was active for the game, the receiver did not play a single offensive snap. McConkey’s return could provide a much-needed boost to quarterback Justin Herbert and a Chargers passing attack that has struggled to establish consistency. While McConkey has been cleared to play, it remains unclear whether he will immediately return to his usual workload after dealing with a lingering foot injury. The Los Angeles Chargers received encouraging news Friday as they prepare for an important AFC West matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs. Los Angeles ultimately suffered a 23-17 loss, continuing a difficult start to the season. Through four appearances this season, McConkey has recorded 12 receptions for 183 yards and one touchdown. Those numbers represent a disappointing start for a receiver who established himself as one of Herbert’s most reliable targets during his first two NFL seasons. However, injuries have played a significant role in limiting his opportunities. The Chargers have also dealt with health concerns involving several other receivers, including Quentin Johnston, Tre’ Harris and Brenen Thompson. Johnston has been managing a chest injury, while Harris suffered a hamstring injury during the loss to Denver. Those setbacks have created additional challenges for Herbert, who has been forced to navigate an offense dealing with injuries at multiple positions. Now, Los Angeles faces another difficult test against Kansas City. Sunday’s matchup against Kansas City presents another challenge for a Chargers team looking to gain momentum in the AFC West. McConkey’s availability gives Justin Herbert a reliable target in the passing game and could provide a much-needed boost to an offense that has struggled with injuries. The Chargers will have to determine how heavily to involve him after his recent injury struggles. For now, Friday’s announcement represents a positive development as Los Angeles prepares to face one of its biggest division rivals. The Houston Texans just got their first win. The Dallas Cowboys can't get out of their own way, and the Buffalo Bills are mauling everyone in their way. It's been a wacky start to the season, which has made our NFL picks and predictions for every game each week a bit more difficult than I expected. We're having to adjust our perceptions and expectations on the fly, and we're still in the mix as we head into what should be a fascinating Week 6. Zach Rotman came out of the bullpen for me last week and came through with a solid week. Many, many thanks to him for helping the cause, but I'm back in the saddle now. Let's hope I don't make this thing go any further off the rails, but let's dive right into this fun slate with our NFL picks for Week 6 as we make predictions both straight-up and against the spread for all 14 games on the slate this week. Toughest NFL Week 6 prediction to make Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Buffalo Bills at Las Vegas Raiders (+5.5) The Buffalo Bills have been rolling, including toppling the Rams in overtime in Los Angeles on Monday night. Stop me if you've heard this one before, but Buffalo has one of the NFL's best offenses behind Josh Allen and it doesn't seem like there's a defense in the league that's going to be able to stop this team from scoring 30 points - they're quite literally averaging 32.7 points per game after the first five games of the year. Meanwhile, the Raiders have certainly fallen back to earth a bit, losing two straight after their 3-0 start to the season. At the same time, the Bills defense is the same problem it's been for the past few years. It seems like Buffalo has to produce at this level offensively to win games because the defense is going to give it up. While the Raiders might not be a surprise contender, they still look like a quite competent football team behind Kirk Cousins and, while Buffalo will be able to score on their defense, they're still averaging 26.4 points per game on the year. I think Buffalo still has the offensive firepower against a middling defense to get the win in this game. But with it being in Vegas against a team that has a legitimate pulse, it's going to be another shootout and one that could likely be decided by a field goal once again. 5.5 points is a bit too many, so we'll take the Raiders against the spread and pray. Easiest NFL Week 6 pick on the board Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Los Angeles Chargers at Kansas City Chiefs (-8.5) This line could've been two touchdowns and I'm still taking the Kansas City Chiefs over the division rival Chargers. For starters, what has LA shown this season to make you believe they have a chance in Arrowhead in Week 6? No, seriously. There's been little evidence to think that this game will be close as the Chiefs have been absolutely rolling on both sides of the ball while Justin Herbert delivers the worst season of his career, the Chargers defense is middling at its best and the self-inflicted wounds in each game from LA multiply likes the heads of a hydra. If that weren't enough, Andy Reid is famously one of the most lethal head coaches when his team is coming off of the bye week. This isn't to say that the Chiefs are a perfect team as I maintain that they still need to find some more upgrades at wide receiver, especially after the gnarly Tyquan Thornton injury. While that may be true, though, they are a far better coached and more talented team than the winless Chargers and I wouldn't be surprised if this game was lopsided and out of hand early in favor of the home side. The pick that probably has you scratching your head Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Dallas Cowboys (+1.5) at Green Bay Packers Coming off of a home loss to undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels and the previously winless Buccaneers, naturally I'm taking the Dallas Cowboys to go on the road to Lambeau and beat the Packers as underdogs. What about this doesn't make sense to you? Yes, the optics look strange. However, this isn't about expecting the Cowboys hiring Mike Pettine to essentially help out new defensive coordinator Christian Parker drastically improving the defense, though it can't hurt. It's more about this being a likely shootout between these two teams because, despite what happened to Tyson Bagent and the Bears, I still don't trust Green Bay on that side of the ball. Furthermore, I also still don't trust the Packers run game, even against Dallas. Expect this game to go back and forth throughout the action, but I believe the Cowboys are going to have more offensive firepower and some adjustments on the side of the ball you can actually trust Dallas on to attack Green Bay throughout. They might not come up with many stops of their own, but they'll have enough to pull out the win. Plus, just from a narrative perspective, if ever there was a time for the Cowboys to keep their fans from abandoning ship, it's a game like this, and this franchise has been masterful at doing exactly that over the years. picks.blurb: Bills vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 6 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Fantasy Basketball Sign Up ALCS Game 4 postponed Ryan Fitzpatrick rips Bo Nix How WNBA Finals will be won Bills vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 6 Tim Crean, ClutchPoints Tue, October 13, 2026 at 8:44 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Buffalo Bills face off against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 6. This matchup between the 4-1 Bills and the 3-2 Raiders gets a prime spot in the late Sunday window as one of the best games of the week. These two original AFC franchises haven't played a game with meaningful stakes for both teams since the 1993 "Just Freeze Baby" Divisional Round game . Now, as both sides come into this game with winning records, let's make some bold Bills-Raiders predictions. Start your Raiders in fantasy football The Bills are their own worst enemy so far this season, as they love to gift their opponents chances to stay in the game. Whether it is shockingly cavalier Josh Allen interceptions, infuriating James Cook fumbles, or the fact that the defense (outside of Deone Walker and Gregory Rousseau) looks like it has no clue what it is doing right now, Buffalo loves keeping the other team in the game. Sunday will be no different, as fans should expect at least two turnovers from the Bills' offense and long stretches where the Raiders' O looks like the 2007 New England Patriots. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) That means big games from the Raiders' defense, Kirk Cousins, Brock Bowers, Ashton Jeanty, and maybe even the likes of Mike Washington Jr., Michael Mayer, and Tre Tucker. So, for all you fantasy football players out there, any Raiders on your roster should be a good play in Week 6 . Josh Allen delivers again Despite the mediocre (or worse) play at times from the Bills' offensive line, wide receivers, tight end, and running backs, and defensive back seven, the Bills are 4-1 and leading the AFC East thanks to one man: Brandon Beane. Just kidding! He's the reason the rest of the team is struggling so much. The real reason is Josh Allen. Through five weeks, Allen is still the betting favorite for NFL MVP this year. Yes, Brock Bowers is playing great, and Patrick Mahomes is back, but if you define MVP as the players whose absence would tank his team's chances the most, Allen has to be the answer. Monday night's dramatic OT win over the preseason Super Bowl favorite Los Angeles Rams came courtesy of 210 yards passing and a staggering 121 yards rushing from the Bills QB. Sure, he threw his obligatory head-scratching pick in the first half, but in the second, it was a one-man battle with 53 Rams players, and the singular man won. Against the Raiders, expect more of the same. Vegas has an improved defense this season and an incredible pass rusher in Maxx Crosby, but that only means Allen will be forced to take off even more as usual. And with his receivers getting minimal separation and Cook's suspect ball security, it will be all Allen, all the time in Week 6. Bills 31, Raiders 24 This won't be a cakewalk for the Bills by any means, as the Raiders are one of (if not) the most improved teams in the league. We know Cousins is a professional QB, the Raiders have some incredible young offensive weapons, and Klint Kubiak seems like a legit NFL head coach with an incredibly bright future. Allen doesn't have those last two things, as his skill position core is the exact same as last year, as long as D.J. Moore is out injured and his "new" head coach is just the same offensive coordinator who couldn't get it done the past three seasons, but with a more impressive title. Nevertheless, Allen should be able to will his Bills to victory over the Raiders in Week 6 just by sheer force of talent and will. As good as Las Vegas has looked at times this season, they are probably a year or two away from being legit contenders. That's why we'll take the Buffalo to win here, and to do so by slightly more than the -5.5-point spread suggests. Buffalo enters the game at 4-1 after an exciting 37-34 overtime victory over the Los Angeles Rams on Monday night. The Raiders, meanwhile, are 3-2 after suffering a 45-17 loss to the New England Patriots. With the Bills carrying one of the league's most productive offenses and Las Vegas looking to bounce back, Sunday's matchup at Allegiant Stadium presents an important test for both teams. Kickoff is scheduled for 4:25 p.m. Eastern on CBS. Josh Allen Leads Buffalo's Explosive Offense Quarterback Josh Allen remains the centerpiece of Buffalo's offense. Through five games, Allen has thrown for 1,249 yards and seven touchdowns while adding eight rushing touchdowns. His ability to create plays with both his arm and legs makes him one of the most difficult quarterbacks to defend. Allen was particularly dangerous against the Rams, throwing for 342 yards and two touchdowns while rushing for 121 yards. His performance helped Buffalo survive a back-and-forth contest and improve to 4-1. Running back James Cook has also been productive, rushing for 532 yards through five games. His speed and ability to create explosive plays give the Bills another weapon that Las Vegas must account for. Head coach Joe Brady will look to keep the offense balanced while helping Allen avoid costly turnovers. Buffalo has committed nine giveaways over its last three games, making ball security an important focus heading into Sunday. Raiders Need a Strong Response Las Vegas will look to quarterback Kirk Cousins to help the offense recover from its disappointing performance against New England. Cousins has thrown for 1,269 yards and 12 touchdowns through five games, giving the Raiders a capable passing attack. Tight end Brock Bowers has been one of Cousins' primary targets, recording 312 receiving yards and three touchdowns. His ability to create mismatches could be especially important against a Buffalo defense that has struggled to contain opposing passing attacks. The Raiders will also rely on running back Ashton Jeanty , who has rushed for 291 yards this season. Establishing the ground game could help Las Vegas control possession and prevent Allen from spending too much time on the field. Head coach Klint Kubiak will need his team to improve its offensive line play and limit mistakes after the loss to New England. A Major Test for Both Teams Buffalo enters the matchup averaging 32.8 points per game, while Las Vegas has averaged 26.4. Both defenses have experienced difficulties, creating opportunities for the offenses to make an impact. The Bills will try to maintain their momentum after the overtime win, while the Raiders need a response at home to remain competitive in the AFC West. With Allen's dual threat ability, Cousins' passing production and two offenses looking to establish control, Sunday's matchup could be an important measuring stick for both teams as the NFL season continues.

LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict Week 6's top games Getty Images We are already in Week 6 of the NFL regular season! Can you believe it? This weekend, two AFC South rivals in the Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars will battle in London, while Caleb Williams looks to return to the lineup against the Atlanta Falcons after missing the last three games. We also have an intriguing matchup in the NFC on Sunday night between the Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers , while the Washington Commanders will look to get back on track against the 49ers in San Francisco following their embarrassing tie with the New York Giants . Dan Quinn needs to find a way to get his team to refocus after they completely forgot about the clock in overtime. Which teams should you pick in Week 6, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 13 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Houston Texans vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (-3) (London) Dajani (Texans +3): The Jaguars have established themselves as one of the best teams in the AFC. While that's objectively true, they certainly aren't perfect. They probably should have dominated a short-handed Philadelphia Eagles team last week, yet didn't. Additionally, there are some questions about the offensive operation. Jacksonville went 0-3 in the red zone last week, including two trips where the Jags failed to score any points from the one-yard line. As for the Texans, they are coming off their first win of the season against the lowly Tennessee Titans . I predict they keep that momentum going and score an upset victory across the pond. DeMeco Ryans is calling defensive plays again, and C.J. Stroud is actually playing good football. He's tied for the most 20-yard completions (21) in the NFL this season. Houston is also 14-2 SU and 11-4-1 ATS in its last 16 divisional games away from home. … Prediction: Texans 21, Jaguars 18 Dubin (Jaguars -3): I think it's a real advantage that the Jaguars have already been in London for a week while the Texans haven't yet traveled across the pond. Jacksonville, as Dajani mentioned, has established itself as one of the best teams in the AFC. The offense has been efficient and explosive, and the defense has looked good as well. I know the Jags struggled with the Eagles for a bit of last week's game and probably should have lost, but Houston has only beaten a Tennessee team that is barely functional. It's not like the Texans have looked good at any point. Their defense has disappointed, and they can't run the ball whatsoever. … Prediction: Jaguars 24, Texans 20 Chicago Bears (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): It looks like Caleb Williams is going to return to the lineup after missing three games with his hamstring injury, and it also looks like Michael Penix Jr . will play after missing the very end of "Sunday Night Football" with his rib injury. The Chicago Bears have racked up their most rushing yards per contest (173.2) through five games since 1988, but keep an eye on the status of Kyle Monangai , who missed Week 5 with a toe injury. Last week's loss to the Packers was concerning from a defensive standpoint. The Bears have actually allowed 30 points over three straight road games (dating back to last year), which is tied for the longest streak in TEAM HISTORY. I'm going to take the points with the home team, and take Bijan Robinson and Co. to bounce back. … Prediction: Falcons 30, Bears 27 Dubin (Bears -3): The impending return of Caleb Williams has me leaning toward Chicago here. In the one non-monsoon game that Williams played, the Bears dropped 59 points on the Panthers . They ran the ball at will and created explosive plays in the passing game. Their defense was exposed a bit by the Packers last week, and the Falcons could get going offensively here ... if Michael Penix Jr. actually plays through the rib injury he suffered last week. At least some of this pick is thinking Tua Tagovailoa could start under center for Atlanta. … Prediction: Bears 23, Falcons 17 Baltimore Ravens (-4.5) at Cleveland Browns Dajani ( Ravens -4.5): I'm not going to bash the Cleveland Browns for their loss to the New York Jets in that gross weather, where punter Corey Bojorquez missed a snap and granted the Jets 34 yards of field position to set up the game-winning touchdown. But I am nervous about Cleveland's injuries with guys like Carson Schwesinger , Mason Graham , Mike Hall Jr., Tytus Howard , Quinshon Judkins and KC Concepcion banged up. Stroud, Green Bay gets its ground game rolling against Dallas, and Justin Herbert breaks out of an ugly slump Getty Images Anything can happen in the NFL , and the start to Week 6 of the 2026 season certainly hammered home that fact. In the Denver Broncos (4-2) 17-14 "Thursday Night Football" overtime win over the Seattle Seahawks , they triumphed at home despite averaging 2.9 yards per play. That's the fewest in Sean Payton's 318-game head-coaching career, and Denver's 168 total yards of offense ranked as their fewest in a victory since Pro Football Hall of Fame quarterback John Elway's first start as a rookie in 1983. Quarterback Bo Nix , who ranks dead last in the NFL in yards per pass attempt at 5.6, improved to a 13-3 career record in games when he averages six yards per pass attempt or fewer, the best of all-time minimum 15 starts per CBS Sports Research, after averaging 4.0 yards per pass attempt on Thursday. All other active quarterbacks have a combined .283 winning percentage in starts where they average six yards per pass attempt or fewer. That's absolutely unfathomable. What other hijinks could take place across the rest of the NFL's Week 6 slate? Here is a look at five bold predictions. Packers run for over 100 yards for first time in 2026 vs. Cowboys The Green Bay Packers are back above .500 after quarterback Jordan Love's laser show (367 yards and 2 passing touchdowns while completing 25 of his 31 throws) in a 31-7 beatdown of the Chicago Bears at Lambeau Field in Week 5. Now that they have a winning record, they're now the owners of the third-fewest rushing yards per game (60.4) by any team above .500 through five games of a season in league history, per CBS Sports Research. Green Bay's NFL-worst rushing offense also ranks as the fewest rushing yards per game through games of any season in the Packers' 106-season franchise history. Some of that has to do with the absence of running back Josh Jacobs , who is on the commissioner's exempt list after being charged with two misdemeanors, and some of that has to do with the team's beat-up offensive line. However, the offensive line has stabilized with veterans Laken Tomlinson and Travis Glover stabilizing the team's guard play. That's one of the reasons why the Packers will run for over 100 yards as a team for the first time in 2026 against the Dallas Cowboys on "Sunday Night Football." The others are that Green Bay running back MarShawn Lloyd is a freight train at 5 feet 9 inches tall and 220 pounds, and the Cowboys have the league's worst run defense (168.4 rushing yards allowed per game). Dallas allowed the Tampa Bay Buccaneers to go off for 241 yards rushing, their most in a game since 2024, on "Thursday Night Football" in Week 5. Facing a leaky defense like that and Lloyd fresh off running through Bears cornerback Jaylon Johnson's face for a touchdown in Week 5, Lloyd and the Packers cross the century mark on the ground for the first time this season. Marshawn Lloyd trucks a guy on his way to the end zone 😤 @CHIvsGB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/NNcSwQfTOU Marvin Harrison Jr. has first 100-yard receiving game since his rookie year Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud is quietly playing efficient football: he has the fifth-most passing attempts without an interception (185) through five games in NFL history while throwing for the fourth-most passing yards in the NFL (1,402) this season. The Texans (1-4) have a high-volume passing offense this season because of their struggling rushing offense, and that will lead to Houston's newest player, 2024 fourth overall pick wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. , thriving in his team debut against the AFC South-leading Jacksonville Jaguars (4-1). How much will he soar in his first game back with his former Ohio State Buckeyes teammate in Stroud? Harrison Jr. will produce his first 100-yard receiving game since his rookie year in 2024 and just the third overall 100-yard receiving game of his young career on Sunday. He and Stroud were Ohio State teammates for two seasons from 2021 to 2022, and Harrison Jr.'s 14 receiving touchdowns when Stroud was the starting quarterback in 2022 are tied for the third most in a single season in Buckeyes' history. Harrison Jr. also set or tied career-highs in catches (77), receiving yards (1,263) and receiving touchdowns (14) in that 2022 season with Stroud. Houston will be celebrating their newest trade acquisition's 100-yard game when the clock hits zero at Wembley Stadium on Sunday. Justin Herbert ends fourth-quarter turnover streak and multi-passing touchdown drought vs. Chiefs The Los Angeles Chargers are injury-plagued and riding the struggle bus at 0-5 to start 2026. Pro Bowl quarterback Justin Herbert is tied for the most interceptions (seven) and turnovers (nine) in the NFL this season, and he has a couple of ugly streaks going against him. He has five consecutive games with a fourth-quarter turnover, making him the first quarterback since Charlie Frye in 2006 to do that. Herbert also hasn't thrown for multiple passing touchdowns in a game in his last seven games, the longest such streak of his career. However, he will play a clean fourth quarter and throw multiple touchdown passes against the 4-0 Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead on Sunday. The last time the Chiefs were on the field in Week 4, 38-year-old Kirk Cousins threw for 365 yards, 2 touchdowns and an interception on 31 of 52 passes in a narrow 30-27 Chiefs win. Herbert will snap out of his funk and raise his level to go toe-to-toe with Mahomes by having a clean fourth quarter and throwing multiple touchdowns for the first time in a while. Jets' Geno Smith throws first interception of 2026 at Patriots Geno Smith is on an incredible public relations campaign in 2026 with the New York Jets . After leading the NFL with 17 interceptions as a Las Vegas Raider in 2025, he hasn't thrown any through five games this season. Smith has six passing touchdowns to no interceptions this season, a stark contrast from his touchdown-to-interception ratio at this time a year ago when he had the same number of touchdown passes (six) but with nine interceptions. He is only the second quarterback in NFL history with no interceptions through five starts, after leading the league in interceptions the previous season, and is tied with Vinny Testaverde, also with the Jets, back in 2001, per CBS Sports Research. However, Smith will throw his first interception of the season in Week 6 at the New England Patriots . Patriots All-Pro cornerback Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) is on track to return this week, fully practicing on Thursday after being limited on Wednesday. In his first game back after a two-game absence, Gonzalez will intercept Smith for the veteran's first interception of 2026. Saints won't cover as road favorite at Giants Yes, your eyes don't deceive you. According to DraftKings Sportsbook , the 1-4 New Orleans Saints are favored by 1.5 points over the 3-1-1 New York Giants on the road at MetLife Stadium. Perhaps the ugliness of the NFC East leader's 27-27 tie at the Washington Commanders in Week 5 is pushing the spread in favor of the Saints. Maybe it's the allure of New Orleans quarterback Tyler Shough , whose 1,299 passing yards rank as the seventh-most in the NFL. Regardless, that positions the Saints to win on Sunday, as they have covered in seven consecutive road games, the longest active road cover streak in the entire NFL, per CBS Sports Research. However, the Saints' road cover streak will be broken on Sunday because Jameis Winston plays a more efficient brand of football than Shough. Sure, Winston's 57.6% is the second-worst in the NFL among 31 qualified quarterbacks in 2026, but he is starting to turn a corner and find a groove as an NFL starting quarterback once again. He is the first Giants quarterback with three-plus passing touchdowns in consecutive games since Eli Manning in 2016, and Winston didn't throw a single interception after having two in Week 4 against the Arizona Cardinals a couple of weeks ago. On the other hand, Shough has a turnover problem: his eight this season are the third-most in the league. away.blurb: Packers list five questionable, rule out four vs. Cowboys | Week 6 Injury Report Skip to main content Primary nav News CB Brandon Cisse (hip) added to injury report, questionable for Sunday night Evan Siegle, packers.com CB Brandon Cisse GREEN BAY – Packers cornerback Brandon Cisse (hip) has been added to the injury report and is among five players who are questionable for Sunday's game against the Dallas Cowboys. The other four questionable are guards Aaron Banks (knee/toe) and Jacob Monk (quadricep), defensive tackle Anthony Campbell (ankle) and receiver Savion Williams (ankle), who's on injured reserve and must be added to the active roster to play. Green Bay ruled out receiver Skyy Moore (ankle), cornerback Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring), and defensive tackles Jonathan Ford (calf) and Javon Hargrave (Achilles). Defensive tackle Jordon Riley (Achilles) is doubtful after returning to practice this week, his first football activity after starting the 2026 season on physically unable to perform. Williams, who was placed on IR with a designation to return at the end of training camp, has been practicing in a limited capacity since the Packers opened his 21-day practice window on Oct. 7. The 2025 third-round pick had 21 touches for 115 total yards with a touchdown as a rookie while serving as Green Bay's kickoff returner. The Packers are thin at wideout right now with Moore out and Jayden Reed 's season over due to a neck injury. "We've done a lot of different things with him dating back to last year, putting him in different positions," said Head Coach Matt LaFleur of Williams on Wednesday. "But I think where he's grown the most is his route-running ability. He's worked really hard at it. He was out there last week running around and he looked pretty good." The Packers are banged-up on the defensive line. In addition to Hargrave suffering a season-ending Achilles injury against Chicago, Ford did not practice this week due to the calf. Campbell hasn't played since injuring his ankle against the New York Jets last month but has practiced in a limited capacity the past two weeks. The Packers only have three other defensive linemen on the 53-man roster at the moment: Devonte Wyatt , Karl Brooks and Chris McClellan . While Cisse's status for Sunday is uncertain, LaFleur confirmed Keisean Nixon will play after sitting out practice Wednesday. The Pro Bowl cornerback has played in 73 consecutive regular-season games since signing with the Packers in 2022. In addition to Nixon, Green Bay did not issue a game status for the following players who will be available: edge Lukas Van Ness (shoulder), safety Evan Williams (illness) and Wyatt (ankle). The Cowboys ruled out cornerback Cobie Durant (hamstring) and tackle Drew Shelton (hamstring), and listed four as questionable: linebacker DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring), defensive tackle L.T. Overton (foot), and cornerbacks Joey Porter Jr. (ankle) and cornerback Ameer Speed (knee). Dallas did not issue a game status

home.headline: NFL releases major update on status of Packers RB Josh Jacobs
home.blurb: The NFL removed Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs from the Commissioner Exempt List, effective Monday, making him eligible to return to the field for Sunday’s Week 7 matchup against the division-rival Detroit Lions. While Jacobs is now eligible to return to the roster, the NFL’s investigation under the league’s Personal Conduct Policy is still underway. Jacobs, who was arrested in May following a domestic disturbance, was originally placed on the Commissioner Exempt List before the 2026 season on Aug. 30. The NFL released a public statement following this move: “The National Football League today notified Josh Jacobs of the Green Bay Packers that he will be removed from the Commissioner Exempt List on Oct. 19. He will be eligible to play in the Packers’ Week 7 game on Oct. 25 after missing six games. “The NFL initiated an investigation under the Personal Conduct Policy following Jacobs’ arrest in May. The league’s review remains ongoing and is not affected by this change to Jacobs’ roster status.” Without Jacobs through the first five games of the 2026 season, the Packers rank dead last in rushing yards per game with 60.4. MarShawn Lloyd has just 112 rushing yards on the season, followed by Kaleb Johnson with 106. The Packers will face off against the Dallas Cowboys in a primetime “Sunday Night Football” matchup in Week 6. home.headline: NFL To Remove Josh Jacobs From Commissioner Exempt List; How Soon Could He Return for Packers?
home.blurb: Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs will be removed from the NFL’s commissioner exempt list on Monday, per an NFL release. He’ll be eligible to return to practice for Week 7. When Might Jacobs Return for Packers? The expectation is that Jacobs’ suspension will be six games. As Matt Schneidman of The Athletic pointed out, if that is indeed the length, he will have already served his time and would still be eligible to return in Week 7 against the Detroit Lions. Shortly after the announcement, Jacobs released a statement through his attorneys. “Josh has dedicated the last several months to bettering himself, and he accepts responsibility for his actions. He is excited to get back to work and on the field with his teammates,” the statement read via Jeremy Fowler of ESPN . “Josh is grateful for the support he is receiving from his teammates, coaches, the Packers organization, and the greatest fans in the world. Since there are ongoing legal matters, he will not have any further comment.” Jacobs pleaded no contest to misdemeanor battery and criminal damage to property charges back in September. He was fined $1,000 plus court fees and can have the property-damage charge dismissed if he meets the agreement’s conditions, including restitution, counseling, supervision, and adhering to a no-contact order with the victim. As already established, the NFL’s investigation is ongoing. The league will probably do so, but the key will be how many games. By all accounts, the Packers are ready to welcome Jacobs back with open arms. After he agreed to the plea deal, head coach Matt LaFleur praised his character, describing the running back’s domestic violence incident as an “ unfortunate situation .”

San Francisco enters the Week 6 matchup at 5-0 after an exciting 32-29 road victory over the Seattle Seahawks, while Washington arrives at 1-3-1 following a frustrating 27-27 overtime tie against the New York Giants. The matchup presents two teams heading in different directions. The 49ers have found ways to win close games, while the Commanders are searching for consistency as they attempt to climb back into the NFC playoff conversation. Kickoff is scheduled for 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN and ABC. Brock Purdy Leads San Francisco's Offense Quarterback Brock Purdy has helped guide the 49ers through an impressive opening stretch. Although San Francisco has faced several challenging opponents, the offense has continued producing at important moments. Purdy threw two touchdown passes against Seattle and helped lead the game-winning drive that set up Eddy Piñeiro's decisive field goal. His ability to distribute the football and make smart decisions has been important to the team's success. Running back Christian McCaffrey remains another major weapon. His versatility as both a runner and receiver gives head coach Kyle Shanahan several ways to attack opposing defenses. San Francisco will look to establish its running game early, create favorable passing situations and control the tempo. The 49ers' offense has also benefited from contributions across the roster, allowing the team to remain productive even when individual drives become difficult. Jayden Daniels Looks to Spark Washington Washington will rely on quarterback Jayden Daniels to help generate offense against a San Francisco defense that has started the season strongly. Daniels demonstrated his playmaking ability against the Giants, rushing for 103 yards and two touchdowns while throwing for 199 yards. However, Washington's inability to finish the game left the team with a disappointing tie. Daniels' mobility could be one of the Commanders' biggest advantages. San Francisco will need disciplined defensive play to prevent him from escaping the pocket and creating explosive gains with his legs. Washington also needs better protection up front and more consistent execution on third downs. Sustaining drives will be particularly important against a 49ers team that has repeatedly capitalized on scoring opportunities. Kyle Shanahan vs. Dan Quinn The coaching matchup adds another layer to Monday night's game. Shanahan has San Francisco playing confident football, while Quinn needs Washington to respond after letting a potential victory slip away. For the Commanders, limiting turnovers and improving their second-half execution will be essential. The 49ers, meanwhile, will look to continue their balanced offensive approach and use their home-field advantage. A Major Test for Both Teams San Francisco has an opportunity to improve to 6-0 and strengthen its position in the NFC West. Washington needs a complete performance to show it can compete with one of the conference's unbeaten teams. With Purdy and McCaffrey leading the 49ers against Daniels and Washington's offense, Monday night's matchup offers an important test for both teams as the NFL season moves deeper into October.

away.blurb: Commanders Prepare for Return of NFL's ‘Next Great' Cornerback The Washington Commanders think they might have a special player in second-year cornerback Trey Amos. The problem is, Amos hasn't been available for quite some time. The Commanders are 1-3-1 and coming off an embarrassing 27-27 tie against the New York Giants , in which Washington let time run out instead of attempting a 41-yard field goal. "SECONDARY REINFORCEMENTS ARE HERE!" DC News Now's Alex Flume wrote on his official X account. " Nick Cross and Trey Amos were out getting involved at Commanders practice Wednesday. Dan Quinn said before practice that they are both expected to practice in full this week. Could be a massive boost for the Commanders pass defense this week." By all accounts, Amos has focused entirely on rehabbing his injury to return to the lineup — something that's taken considerably longer than anyone anticipated. "Dan Quinn said CB Trey Amos tweaked his ankle while in coverage on a deep ball to Terry McLaurin the other day," The Athletic's Nicki Jhabvala wrote on her official X account on August 10. "Quinn said he'll know more in a day or so about his timetable to return." Unlock the latest Heavy on Commanders news — direct to your inbox. Updated Oct 16, 2026 at 11:27pm Amos has missed 12 consecutive regular-season games since Week 10 of his rookie season, when he fractured his fibula against the Detroit Lions . Now, when the Commanders may need him most, Amos looks like he'll be back and will make his comeback in a Week 6 primetime showdown against the unbeaten San Francisco 49ers on Monday Night Football. Play Trey Amos: Total Focus on Returning to Commanders "Trey Amos has no hobbies," Commanders reporter Ben Standig wrote on his official X account. "No distractions. Just football. After 11 months and two injuries, the Commanders CB wants his life back." Amos was coming into his own when he got injured — he made 8 starts in 10 games as a rookie. The Commanders have had one glaring weakness on their defense this season and it's been with 3r-dyear cornerback Mike Sainristil . Getting Amos back and healthy could put Amos, Amik Robertson , and Rasul Douglas at two outside cornerback spots and one slot cornerback spot. That would be the best-case scenario — mainly because it keeps Sainristil off the field. "My big question for MNF, assuming Trey Amos can play: is Amik going back to nickel? Or is he playing outside until it's nickel package and then sliding inside? Amik's been stellar outside, but Trey and Rasul are two of your three best corners, and neither are playing inside," The Full Command Show wrote on its official X account. Amos started training camp on the PUP list but returned to practice a few weeks later … and automatically got hurt again. Kyle Shanahan told reporters, including ESPN's Nick Wagoner , that Mike Evans is dealing with an Achilles injury and also has a rib issue. 49ers get concerning Mike Evans report amid Achilles injury issue - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL 49ers get concerning Mike Evans report amid Achilles injury issue Matt Sullivan Thu, October 15, 2026 at 8:33 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Sitting at 5-0 through five weeks, there are a lot of things to like about the San Francisco 49ers . But that doesn't mean there aren't things to worry about. Over the last few years, there might not be a team more hampered by injuries than the 49ers. Once again, these injury issues are hitting the 49ers hard. Through five weeks, the 49ers' wide receiver room has been tested in a big way. Mike Evans dealing with Achilles injury amid uncertain Week 6 status "49ers WR Mike Evans won't practice today," Wagoner reports. "He is dealing with Achilles soreness, per Kyle Shanahan. That's in addition to a rib issue." Evans is not only dealing with a rib injury, but he also has soreness in his Achilles, which is a very worrying update for the 49ers wide receiver. Achilles injuries are season-ending, though in this case it's not actually an Achilles tear. But that doesn't mean it's not a concerning situation for the 49ers offense. They recently lost Samuel to a multi-week hamstring injury, and now there's some concern about Evans' status going forward. MORE : Mike Evans trolls Trevon Diggs with classic 'Who are you?' jersey check in viral exchange It's still early in the week for the 49ers, with their Monday Night Football matchup against the Washington Commanders giving Evans some time to get right. But, considering the 49ers are already without De'Zhaun Stribling, Ricky Pearsall, and Demarcus Robinson, and Christian Kirk isn't guaranteed to come back this week, losing Evans would be a huge deal for the 49ers. As of now, their only healthy wide receivers are Brandin Cooks, Jordan Watkins and Brandin Cooks. If Evans and Kirk don't play in Week 6, the 49ers are going to have a very depleted wide receiver room. It's too soon to tell if Evans will actually miss Week 6, but this Achilles injury update is something worth worrying about for the 49ers, considering all of the bad injury luck this team has right now. By Michael Gallagher Sports Content Coordinator 0 Share Newsweek is a Trust Project member See more of our trusted coverage when you search. Prefer Newsweek on Google to see more of our trusted coverage when you search. The San Francisco 49ers have had arguably the worst injury luck of any team in the NFL this season. More than 15 players are currently on the reserve/injured list while a handful of others are expected to miss some time with their respective ailments. San Francisco’s defense has been hit particularly hard, and star edge-rusher Nick Bosa’s absence over the last few weeks has been noticeable. Keion White has done his part to pick up the slack, but the rest of San Francisco’s pass-rush has left much to be desired, which is why Kristopher Knox of Bleacher Report believes the 49ers should make an all-in move to upgrade the position. Knox recently suggested the 49ers execute a trade with the winless Los Angeles Chargers for Pro Bowler Khalil Mack. “Los Angeles fell to 0-5 on Sunday, while Mack continues to be a legitimate difference-maker,” Knox wrote . “… Mack is playing on a one-year deal and should be interested in playing for a team that could get him his first career playoff win. “.. Mack should be the top target for any team with Super Bowl aspirations that happens to need help rushing opposing passers. It'll be a fairly significant surprise if he remains in Los Angeles beyond next month's deadline.” Despite multiple reports indicating the Chargers would want a fifth-round pick in exchange for Mack, Knox suggested it could take at least a conditional 2027 fourth-round pick to get a deal finalized given the demand for strong pass-rushers from contending teams. Through five games this season, Mack has logged 14 pressures, eight hurries, five tackles for loss, three QB hits, and three sacks with a pass-rush win-rate of 9.5%, according to Pro Football Focus. Adding that kind of production opposite White would be a big boost for the 49ers in the interim, and once Bosa comes back, it would make SF’s pass-rush all the more dangerous come playoff time.
